input.name: Silicon Motion
input.thesis: NAND controller maker gaining share as NAND makers exit low-priority segments; Q2 2026 revenue +127% YoY, guiding to more than double 2026 revenue; second-tier beneficiary of the NAND shortage after SanDisk.

dossier.name: Silicon Motion Technology Corp (ADS)
dossier.market_cap: ≈ $8.7B (33.9M ADS × ~$256 close on Sep 4, 2026; ≈ $8.0B at the Sep 3 close of $235.82). StockAnalysis showed $8.62B at an undated point in late Aug/early Sep.
dossier.business: Silicon Motion is a Taiwan-based fabless designer of NAND-flash controller ICs: client PCIe SSD controllers (~30% share of client PC SSD controllers, targeting 40%), eMMC/UFS embedded controllers for smartphones, IoT and automotive, and MonTitan PCIe Gen5/Gen6 enterprise SSD controllers for hyperscalers. Customers are NAND makers (Micron, SanDisk, SK hynix, Kioxia, YMTC), SSD module makers, PC/phone OEMs and, increasingly, cloud service providers; the top five customers are a majority of sales (2025 20-F). It also sells finished storage "solutions" — Ferri industrial/automotive SSDs and enterprise boot drives (including for Nvidia BlueField DPUs) — where it buys NAND and integrates its own controller; that line was ~30% of Q2 2026 revenue after growing ~1,600-1,700% YoY.
dossier.why_now: The bottleneck is NAND flash, not SIMO. AI data-center demand has absorbed supply: 2026 NAND capacity is reported sold out industry-wide, TLC 1Tb pricing roughly doubled in six months ($4.80 to $10.70), NAND prices rose 55-60% QoQ in Q1 2026, lead times exceeded 20 weeks, NAND makers are steering 70-80% of output to data center by 2027, and SIMO's SVP said in June 2026 that "the retail SSD market has almost disappeared." SIMO benefits second-hand in three ways: (1) NAND makers de-prioritise client SSD, mobile eMMC/UFS and boot drives, so module makers and OEMs that buy merchant controllers take share — SIMO's eMMC/UFS revenue roughly doubled YoY in Q2 and client SSD share is heading from ~30% toward 40%; (2) PCIe Gen5 mix lifts controller ASP (SSD controller revenue +50-55% YoY in Q2 despite PC units guided down 5-10%); (3) its solutions business sells finished drives at inflated NAND prices, which is why Ferri/boot drives went from a rounding error to ~30% of revenue. Management says supply gets "even worse" in 2027, and MonTitan (2 Tier-1 customers in production, 5 more CSPs ramping in H2 2026, 5-10% of revenue exiting 2026) adds a data-center leg. The sceptical point: the headline "more than double 2026 revenue" guide is arithmetically locked — H1 was $793.1M and the Q3 guide midpoint is $530M, so Q4 only needs to exceed ~$448M (vs. a Q3 guide of $519-541M) to double 2025's $885.6M. That datapoint is no longer new information.
dossier.analogue: Closest to the 2026 bottleneck-play family (SanDisk/Micron/Seagate) but only loosely — it is a second-derivative beneficiary, not the owner of the sold-out input. Three mismatches with the template: (1) earnings multiplier is ~2.5x (Q2 non-GAAP EPS $2.43 vs ~$0.69 a year ago; 2026E EPS ~$9 vs FY2025 GAAP ~$3.6), not the 7x-21x SanDisk/Micron delivered; (2) SIMO has no pricing power of its own on the scarce good — it captures volume/share and passes NAND inflation through its ~30% solutions line, which makes it a NAND buyer at peak prices ($673M inventory, H1 operating cash flow −$95M); (3) the multiple has already re-rated to ~26-28x forward, so it has the share-gain volume story of the Dell analogue but at a bottleneck-owner's multiple rather than a low one. It is not a binary readout and not government-backed. Best description: a bottleneck-adjacent share-gain story that the market has priced like a bottleneck owner.

dossier.guidance: Given Jul 29, 2026 with Q2 results: Q3 2026 revenue $519-541M (+15-20% QoQ; ~+114-123% YoY vs $242.0M), gross margin 50-51%, operating margin 27.5-28.5%, with growth across nearly all product lines led by Ferri automotive, enterprise boot drives and MonTitan. Full year 2026: record revenue, "more than double" 2025 (i.e., >$1.77B); MonTitan to be 5-10% of revenue exiting 2026; five additional Tier-1 CSP MonTitan customers (3 Asia, 2 US) to begin ramping in H2 2026; 4nm PCIe Gen6 MonTitan tape-out in August 2026 with design wins at 2 NAND makers plus several CSPs; benefit from Nvidia BlueField-4 boot-drive ramp in H2 2026. Consensus 2026 revenue has moved from $1.63B to $1.87B (Simply Wall St), which implies Q4 ≈ $545M, roughly flat-to-up 3% on the Q3 midpoint. Earlier context (Apr 28, Q1 call): PC units −5-10% in 2026, mobile/eMMC-UFS could reach 35-40% of revenue over time, NAND supply secured from three makers. SIMO management (Computex, June 2026): NAND supply gets "even worse" in 2027, 70-80% of NAND to data centers by 2027.
dossier.valuation: At ~$256 (Sep 4, 2026 close, from lower-quality quote sources; $235.82 on Sep 3 per StockAnalysis), market cap ≈ $8.7B on ~33.9M ADS. Forward P/E ≈ 28x consensus 2026E EPS ($8.96-9.04) and ≈ 21-22x 2027E ($11.5-12.0); on the Sep 3 price, ~26x / ~20x. Third-party snapshots: 32.2x forward (GuruFocus, Jun 13, 2026), 30x at $272 (Simply Wall St, early Aug 2026) vs. a 31x US semiconductor average. EV ≈ $8.6B after netting the $1.15B convert against ~$1.25B pro-forma cash, i.e. ~4.6x consensus 2026E sales of $1.87B. Peers: Phison ~33x forward (Simply Wall St) vs. 23x Taiwan semis; SanDisk valued by Goldman at 20x "normalized" EPS. History: SIMO spent 2023-2025 in a low-to-mid-teens forward P/E (not verified this session), so the multiple has roughly doubled while EPS has ~2.5x'd — the "multiple re-rate" leg of the framework has already happened. GuruFocus GF Value ($112.69) and Simply Wall St fair value ($157) both flag overvaluation; the sell side (avg PT $366-370, range $325-450, all 9-12 analysts Buy) does not. Verdict: the 2026 doubling and most of 2027 consensus are in the price; the multiple already embeds the thesis, and the stock only works from here if 2027 EPS lands ≥$12 and the market keeps paying 20x+ at what may be peak NAND-cycle margins.

dossier.how_far_run_note: The stated thesis (Q2 +127%, 2026 revenue more than doubling) is fully in the price: the doubling is arithmetically locked by the Q3 guide, consensus already sits at $1.87B, every covering analyst is at Buy, and the forward multiple has roughly doubled from its 2023-25 range to ~26-28x. What is only partly priced is 2027 — the NAND shortage extending/worsening, MonTitan reaching 5-10% of revenue with seven Tier-1 customers, PCIe Gen6 wins — where 2027 EPS estimates are still being revised up (+14.6% in 60 days) and the stock is 28% off its high with the convert overhang absorbed. Late-cycle features to respect: peak-ish margins on a peak multiple, a $673M NAND inventory bet, and consumer end-markets that are shrinking. Net: mid, leaning late; upside now depends on Q4/2027 guidance beats, not on the 2026 numbers.

dossier.bull_case: NAND stays sold out through 2027 (SIMO, Goldman and Gartner all say relief is late-2027 at the earliest), so NAND makers keep ceding client SSD, mobile and boot-drive sockets to module makers/OEMs using merchant controllers; SIMO takes client SSD share from ~30% to 40% and mobile becomes 35-40% of revenue. Revenue runs ~$1.9-2.0B in 2026 (Q3 $530M midpoint, Q4 ~$545M) and $2.3-2.5B in 2027 with gross margin holding 50-51% and operating margin 28-30% as MonTitan (5-10% of revenue exiting 2026, seven Tier-1 customers, Gen6 wins at two NAND makers) lifts mix. That yields 2027 EPS of $12-14; at 25x the stock is $300-350, matching the $325-450 sell-side range and offering 20-35% upside from ~$256. The $1.15B zero-coupon convert funds the NAND inventory needed to keep the solutions business (~30% of sales) growing without near-term dilution below $380.50, and the "transformation into an AI-infrastructure storage supplier" narrative gives the multiple a reason to hold. Short interest of 1.2% means any Q4 guide above ~$560M meets little resistance.
dossier.bear_case: (1) SIMO has become a NAND buyer at the top: inventory rose 60% in six months to $673M (about 1.5 quarters of sales) and H1 operating cash flow was −$95M; if NAND contract prices roll over — memory cycles turn abruptly and DRAM/NAND capex is accelerating — the ~30% solutions line deflates and inventory gets written down against a 50% gross margin. (2) It is gaining share of shrinking pies: PC units guided −5-10%, smartphones weak on component inflation, and the retail SSD market has "almost disappeared"; once NAND makers regain capacity they re-enter with captive controllers (Samsung ~20-25% controller share, SK hynix/Micron ~15%), reversing the very share gains driving eMMC/UFS +100%. (3) Multiple risk: ~28x 2026E EPS on cyclically high margins; if 2027 EPS is $9 rather than $12 and the multiple reverts to 15x, the stock is ~$135, −47%. (4) Overhang: $1.15B of converts due 2031 (~3.0M ADS, ~9% dilution above $380.50) that knocked the stock 8-10% on announcement, plus top-five customer concentration. (5) The "more than double" guide is already locked by Q3 guidance, so the next print must deliver a strong Q4 guide to avoid a "peak growth" sell-off; a flat Q4 guide (~$530M) would show sequential growth stalling from +32%/+15-20%.
dossier.what_confirms: Q3 2026 print (~Nov 4): revenue at or above the $541M top end AND a Q4 guide of ≥$560M with gross margin guided ≥51% and operating margin ≥29%, MonTitan confirmed at ≥5% of Q4 revenue with the five additional CSP customers in production, and operating cash flow turning positive as inventory begins converting — together with Micron (Sep 30) and SanDisk (Nov 5) reiterating that NAND is sold out through 2027 with contract prices still rising. That combination would show the share gains are structural and that 2027 EPS ≥$12 is plausible.
dossier.what_kills: Any of: a Q4 guide at or below the Q3 guide range (≤$541M) or gross-margin guide below 50%; an inventory write-down or a disclosed NAND allocation shortfall for Ferri/boot drives; TrendForce/Micron/SanDisk data showing NAND contract prices falling QoQ before mid-2027; NAND makers announcing re-entry into client/mobile with captive controllers; MonTitan slipping below 5% of revenue exiting 2026 or customer ramps pushed to 2027; operating cash flow still negative in Q3 after a $1.15B raise. The single cleanest kill is a sequential revenue decline guided for Q4 2026.
dossier.balance_sheet: Jun 30, 2026: cash and equivalents $74.4M plus $107.4M restricted cash; $59.2M short-term bank loans under revolving facilities; inventory $673.0M (vs $421.8M at Dec 31, 2025); shareholders' equity $1.05B. H1 2026 operating cash flow −$95.0M (vs +$33.0M in H1 2025) as NAND purchases for Ferri/boot drives absorbed cash; H1 dividends paid $33.9M ($0.50/ADS quarterly, ~$2.00 annualized, ~0.8% yield); no buybacks in 2026. Post-quarter: $1.15B of 0.00% convertible senior notes due Aug 15, 2031 closed Aug 13, 2026 (initial $800M, upsized; conversion price $380.50 = 65% premium to $230.61 on Aug 10; principal to be repaid in cash, excess in cash/ADS at company election; no capped call found), proceeds for general corporate purposes and to repay the credit agreement. Pro forma: roughly $1.25B of cash against $1.15B of converts, i.e. approximately net-cash neutral, but the equity now carries $1.15B of debt and ~3.0M ADS (~9%) of potential dilution above $380.50. Cash burn is working-capital-driven rather than structural; the test is whether Q3/Q4 operating cash flow turns positive. Share count ~33.9M ADS; insider sales in 2026 have been small (director 2,000 shares in June; Form 144s for 1,500 and 10,500 shares).
dossier.suggested_sizing: Speculative sleeve 1-1.5%, not core. Add only on a post-Q3 pullback with a Q4 guide ≥$560M and positive operating cash flow; cap at 2%. Do not size as a bottleneck-owner trade — the earnings multiplier is ~2.5x, not 7-21x, and the multiple has already re-rated.

skeptic.priced_in: Largely. The stock is up ~186% over 12 months and has more than doubled YTD; the "more than double 2026 revenue" guide is arithmetically locked by the Q3 guide ($519-541M on top of $793M H1), consensus already sits at ~$1.87B, and the forward multiple has re-rated to ~26-28x 2026E (66x trailing, 9x trailing sales per Motley Fool/Simply Wall St, which flags it ~47% overvalued). Sell-side PTs (~$341 avg per MarketBeat) still imply ~30% upside from ~$256, but the dossier itself concedes the stock only works if 2027 EPS lands at or above $12 on a 20x+ multiple at what may be peak NAND-cycle margins. The Sep 4 +8.7% bounce was on generic "NAND demand" optimism, not new data. What is not fully priced is 2027 (MonTitan mix, Gen6 wins, share gains persisting), but that is also where the estimate dispersion is widest ($8.86-18.42).
skeptic.durability: The input bottleneck looks durable into 2027: Phison's CEO (Bloomberg, Sep 2; Digitimes Jun 23 and Aug 14) says orders are booked into 2Q27, the worst NAND shortage comes in 2027, and no new fabs land before late 2027; TrendForce shows 2026 NAND capex only ~+5% with Samsung/SK hynix prioritising HBM/DRAM, Kioxia/SanDisk +41% but on BiCS8/9 ramps. SK hynix Yongin phase 1 targets 1Q27 and Samsung V10 slipped into 2026, so meaningful relief is a late-2027 event. However, NAND contract price momentum is decelerating fast per TrendForce: +55-60% QoQ in 1Q26, +70-75% in 2Q26, but only +10-15% guided for 3Q26 as consumer demand weakens and base effects bite. That matters for SIMO specifically because ~30% of revenue is now finished drives (Ferri/boot) sold at inflated NAND prices off a $673M inventory bought near peak; the volume/share-gain leg (client SSD, eMMC/UFS) is more durable than the price pass-through leg. SIMO does not own the scarce good, and when NAND makers regain capacity they can re-enter with captive controllers. Durability of the share gains is plausible through 2027; durability of 50%+ gross margin and the solutions mix is not.
skeptic.evidence_quality: Good on the core numbers: Q2 revenue $451M (+127% YoY, vs $198.7M) and Q3 guide $519-541M / GM 50-51% / OM 27.5-28.5% are confirmed by Zacks, Investing.com and the 6-K; the $1.15B 0% 2031 convert at $380.50 (65% premium to $230.61) with $1.127B net proceeds is confirmed by the closing release and SEC exhibits. The dossier is honest about its weak spots (Sep 4 price from low-quality sources, derived YTD base, back-solved prior-year EPS, unverified historical P/E). Gaps found: it omits the TrendForce 2Q26 (+70-75%) and 3Q26 (+10-15%) contract-price data that directly bears on the solutions-line and inventory risk; it did not surface the late-August analyst downgrade or the Sep 1 -5.3% day; capped-call absence remains unconfirmed (my search also found no mention); and the convert's issuer call from Aug 20, 2029 at 130% of conversion price is missing. Backlog/book-to-bill and customer-concentration percentages remain unknown.
corrections: Valuation section says 'all 9-12 analysts Buy'; AAII (as of Aug 31, 2026) records one analyst downgrade and zero upgrades in the prior month, and the stock fell ~5.3% on Sep 1 and 6.85% on another late-Aug/early-Sep session. Rating consensus is no longer unanimous.
Convert net proceeds are disclosed, not estimated: $1.127B after initial purchasers' discounts and before expenses (closing release / 6-K). Replace the '~$1.12-1.13B assuming ~2% fees' estimate.

Convert terms omit the issuer redemption right: notes are callable for cash on or after Aug 20, 2029 if the ADS price is at or above 130% of the $380.50 conversion price (~$495). Add to balance_sheet.

why_now cites only 1Q26 NAND contract pricing (+55-60% QoQ). TrendForce data show 2Q26 at +70-75% QoQ and a 3Q26 forecast of only +10-15% QoQ, with consumer demand weakening; pricing momentum is decelerating sharply, which is material to the ~30% solutions line and the $673M inventory.

Add to durability evidence: Phison CEO says NAND orders are booked into 2Q27 and 2027 will be the worst shortage year (Digitimes Jun 23 / Aug 14; Bloomberg Sep 2), and Phison is demanding customer pre-payment; TrendForce shows 2026 NAND capex ~+5% YoY with Samsung/SK hynix diverting to HBM/DRAM. This strengthens the bottleneck-durability leg but not SIMO's pricing power.

Trailing valuation context missing: Motley Fool (Sep 3) cites ~66.6x trailing P/E and ~9.3x trailing P/S; the dossier's 4.6x is EV/forward-sales. Both should be shown to avoid understating how rich the stock screens on reported numbers.
skeptic.one_line: SIMO: real share-gain story on a durable 2027 NAND shortage, but the 2026 doubling is locked and priced at ~28x forward; NAND price momentum decelerating (+10-15% Q3 vs +70-75% Q2) threatens the 30% solutions line and $673M inventory — watch Q4 guide (need >$560M) and OCF turn on ~Nov 4.

input.name: Winbond Electronics
input.thesis: Specialty DRAM and NOR flash maker with capacity sold out for 2026 and 2027 and DRAM prices expected to rise roughly 4x; the closest structural analogue to SanDisk one tier down.

dossier.name: Winbond Electronics Corp.
dossier.market_cap: ~NT$783bn (~US$25bn at ~NT$31/USD, FX not verified) on 4.50bn shares at NT$174.00 close, 5 Sep 2026 (Investing.com / stockanalysis.com). Stockopedia showed NT$816.75bn at a NT$181.50 close in early September, so the figure moves ~5% day to day.
dossier.business: Winbond is a Taiwanese IDM that makes specialty/legacy DRAM (DDR3, DDR4, LPDDR4, sold as "Customized Memory Solutions", 53% of 2Q26 revenue) and code-storage flash (NOR flash, where it is global #1 with ~23% share, plus SLC NAND; flash was 33% of 2Q26 revenue) on its own 20-25nm and now 16nm fabs in Taichung and Kaohsiung. Customers are industrial, automotive, networking, consumer-electronics and increasingly AI-server/data-centre OEMs and module makers that still need DDR4/DDR3 and boot NOR after the Big 3 (Samsung, SK Hynix, Micron) shifted wafers to HBM/DDR5. Roughly 50% of DRAM shipments are now under 1-2 year LTAs with quarterly price resets.
dossier.why_now: This is a classic 2026 bottleneck play, one tier below SanDisk/Micron: the Big 3 and CXMT vacated DDR4/DDR3/LPDDR4 to chase HBM, leaving Nanya and Winbond as the residual suppliers of a product that AI servers, networking gear and industrial/auto still consume. Winbond said in February 2026 that DRAM prices would reach roughly 4x mid-2025 levels by June 2026 and that capacity for 2026 and 2027 was already fully sold out (TrendForce, 11 Feb 2026); TrendForce data since then show DDR4 8Gb contract prices at an all-time high of US$25 in August 2026 and NOR flash contract prices up 100-120% in 1H26. The result shows up in the P&L with almost no lag: revenue went from NT$20.0bn in 1Q25 to NT$59.8bn in 2Q26, gross margin from 35% (FY25) to 66.2%, and quarterly EPS from a loss to NT$5.40 (2Q26) versus NT$0.88 for all of 2025. On the 6 Aug 2026 call management said contract prices were still rising in 3Q, operating margin would exceed 50%, 2027 supply would be even tighter, and customers were asking for LTAs out to 2029-2030 with prepayment of fab construction costs. The open question is not whether the spike happened (it did, and the stock is up ~8x in 12 months) but how long it lasts and whether the market will pay more than a ~6-8x run-rate multiple for it.
dossier.analogue: Bottleneck play, closest to SanDisk (sold-out input, 3-4x price spike, earnings up >20x, multiple re-rated) and the fit is tight on mechanics: FY25 EPS NT$0.88 versus a 2Q26 single-quarter EPS of NT$5.40 and a plausible 2026 EPS of NT$20-25, i.e. a 20-28x earnings step-up, and the stock has re-rated from a 200x+ trailing P/E to ~6-8x on run-rate. Three differences keep it "one tier down": (1) the scarcity is in a vacated legacy niche (DDR4/DDR3/NOR) rather than an AI-critical input like HBM/enterprise NAND, so it is more exposed to re-entry (Samsung and SK Hynix already extended DDR4 production into 2026-27; CXMT is targeting 420k wpm in 2027); (2) consumer-facing DRAM pricing momentum is already decelerating (TrendForce: 3Q26 increases moderating to 13-18% QoQ, 4Q26 converging further); (3) it trades in a retail-heavy Taiwan market with limit-up/limit-down days and disposition-stock curbs, so the beta is higher than the fundamentals. Not a Dell-style volume play (it is a price play), not binary, not government-backed.

dossier.bull_case: Contract prices keep rising through 4Q26 (JPMorgan modelled +~50% QoQ for DDR3/DDR4 in 3Q26), July's NT$26.8bn holds through September, and 3Q26 prints ~NT$80bn revenue, >50% operating margin and ~NT$7+ EPS, with 4Q26 higher again as Kaohsiung ramps toward 24K wpm. LTAs through 2029-2030 with customer prepayment would convert a spike into a multi-year annuity and justify re-rating from ~6x toward the 10x that a "structural" specialty supplier could command; 10x NT$30 = NT$300, in line with the JPMorgan NT$360 target and 70%+ above the current price. dossier.bear_case: Legacy DRAM is a vacated niche, not a moat. Samsung and SK Hynix have already extended DDR4 production into 2026-27 (SK Hynix boosting output at Wuxi) because DDR4 briefly priced above DDR5; CXMT is planning 420k wpm by 2027 and its exit from DDR4 was policy-driven and reversible; Morgan Stanley's downgrade to Equal-weight (target NT$140, 20% below the current price) was explicitly a CXMT-supply call. TrendForce already sees consumer DRAM price tolerance "at its limit", 3Q26 increases moderating to 13-18% QoQ and 4Q26 converging further, with NAND turning to surplus in 2H27. Winbond itself is adding ~60% wafer capacity and doubling bits into that; if DDR4 contract prices fall 30-40% from a US$25 peak during 2027 while its bits rise 50%, revenue is flat-to-down and gross margin falls from 66% toward 40-45%, taking EPS from ~NT$22 to perhaps NT$10-12; a cyclical trough multiple of 8-10x on that is NT$80-120, or 30-55% downside. The stock has already shown the fragility: limit-down on 28 Jul 2026 on Korean memory-stock panic, and it is 25% below its June high after two record quarters, i.e. beats are no longer moving it.
dossier.what_confirms: August and September monthly revenue at or above NT$26-27bn (3Q26 revenue at or above ~NT$78-80bn, +30% QoQ) together with 3Q26 operating margin above 50% on the early-November call, and a TrendForce 4Q26 forecast that still shows DDR4/DDR3 contract prices rising QoQ. dossier.what_kills: A first quarter-on-quarter decline in DDR4/DDR3 contract prices (TrendForce 4Q26 or 1Q27 forecast), or a monthly revenue print rolling back below June's NT$20.6bn while capacity is rising, which would mean price is falling faster than bits are growing. Secondary killers: confirmation that Samsung/SK Hynix are re-expanding DDR4 wafer starts into 2027, CXMT resuming DDR4 exports at scale, or customers deferring LTA pulls (rising customer inventory days), any of which converts the sold-out claim into a take-or-pay dispute.

skeptic.priced_in: Largely. The stock is up roughly 8x in 12 months, the management call for ~4x DRAM prices by June 2026 has essentially played out (DDR4 8Gb contract at a record ~US$25 in August), and the market has already compressed the multiple to ~6-8x run-rate earnings, the same peak-cycle discount applied to Micron and SanDisk. The tell is that the stock sits ~25% below its 22 June high (NT$233.50) despite a record 2Q26 (revenue +185% YoY, GM 66%, EPS NT$5.40) and a record July (NT$26.8bn): beats are no longer moving it, which means the market is trading duration, not 2026 numbers. Consensus (NT$16 for 2026) does look stale versus H1 EPS of NT$7.65 plus a July run-rate implying NT$7+ for 3Q alone, so there is room for upward estimate drift, but a re-rating requires evidence that 2027 pricing is contracted rather than spot. Search snippets confirm the 5 Sep price (NT$174), 52-week range (22.75-233.50) and consensus target (NT$247.57, 7 Buys), so the price framing in the dossier is accurate.
skeptic.durability: This is the weak leg. The scarcity is in a vacated legacy niche (DDR4/DDR3/LPDDR4/NOR), and the two big swing factors both cut against duration: Samsung and SK Hynix have extended DDR4 production into 2027 because fully depreciated legacy lines are unusually profitable at these prices, and CXMT is doubling DRAM wafer capacity to >500k wpm by 2028 (it says it exits DDR4 in 2026, but that is a policy decision that can reverse). TrendForce's own trajectory is decelerating: 45-50% QoQ in 2Q26, single- to low-double-digit in 3Q26, 4Q26 "converging further" with weak end demand and elevated inventories cited, though it still expects supplier capacity shifts toward server/HBM to stop contract prices from actually falling. Winbond is adding ~60% wafers (Kaohsiung 15K to 24K wpm) and 16nm into that, so the 2027 equation is bits up 50%+ against prices that at best go flat. Two things partially offset this and one of them is missing from the dossier: (1) the ~50% of DRAM shipments under 1-2 year LTAs with customers asking for 2029-30 terms and prepayment, and (2) TSMC's July 2026 collaboration with Winbond on Wafer-on-Wafer 3D stacking using Winbond's CUBE DRAM for AI chips, which is the first evidence of Winbond being pulled into an AI-critical supply chain rather than just a residual legacy supplier. That deal is probably what lies behind the unsourced "Nvidia supply chain" line and deserves its own section. Net: durable for 2-3 more quarters, genuinely uncertain for 2027, and the first QoQ DDR4 contract-price decline remains the correct thesis breaker.
skeptic.evidence_quality: Good on the reported numbers, mixed on the analyst and price-series layer. The 2Q26 revenue, gross margin, and July revenue figures are confirmed by StorageNewsletter/DigiTimes snippets; the current price, 52-week range and consensus are confirmed by Investing.com. The analyst is candid about gaps (2Q26 balance sheet not found, YTD not verified, no like-for-like 4x price series, dividend not reconciled) and these were not resolvable from snippets either, so the balance-sheet "near net cash" claim is inference, not fact, and should be treated as such. Two specific weaknesses: the Morgan Stanley rating sequence is used inconsistently (the bear case cites the March Equal-weight/NT$140 call as if current, but MS upgraded to Overweight NT$222 in June, after that downgrade), and the TrendForce 3Q26 consumer DRAM increase is quoted as 13-18% QoQ while another TrendForce note gives 8-13% for the overall 3Q26 hike, so the dossier should pin which segment it means. The August monthly revenue (due by 10 Sep) had not been released as of the search, so the "does July's NT$26.8bn hold" test is still live. The omission of the TSMC WoW/CUBE partnership is the largest evidence gap.
corrections: Morgan Stanley rating sequence: the downgrade to Equal-weight (stock limit-down to NT$110 on 20 Mar 2026, thesis that the DDR4 rally slows in 2H26) came BEFORE the June 2026 upgrade to Overweight with a NT$222 target (bull NT$264). The bear case cites the NT$140 EW target as if it were the live view; the latest found MS stance is Overweight NT$222.

TrendForce 3Q26 DRAM price forecast: the dossier says consumer DRAM increases moderate to 13-18% QoQ; a TrendForce note in the search results gives an overall 3Q26 hike of ~8-13% QoQ (after 45-50% in 2Q26). Specify which product category the 13-18% refers to or use the 8-13% figure.

Missing material item: TSMC announced (early July 2026) a collaboration with Winbond on Wafer-on-Wafer 3D stacking, with Winbond supplying CUBE-architecture DRAM wafers to be stacked with TSMC logic wafers for AI chips, framed by industry as TSMC building a domestic memory supply chain. This is not in the dossier and is likely the source of the unsourced 'Nvidia supply chain' claim; it should be added to why_now/bull_case and catalysts.

CXMT capacity: the dossier cites 420k wpm by 2027; reports also put CXMT at over 500k wpm by 2028 (doubling), and CXMT has stated it will stop producing DDR4 in 2026. Both the larger capacity number and the explicit DDR4 exit should be reflected in the bear case (re-entry risk is a policy reversal, not a current plan).

Balance sheet: 'at or near net cash by mid-2026' is inference from H1 net income vs capex, not a reported figure; the latest hard data is still 30 Sep 2025. Label it explicitly as an estimate in balance_sheet rather than only in unverified_claims.
skeptic.one_line: Winbond (2344 TT): legacy DRAM/NOR bottleneck play, ~8x in 12 months and 25% off the June high at ~6-8x run-rate EPS; 2026 is priced, 2027 hinges on DDR4 contract prices holding vs Samsung/SK Hynix/CXMT re-entry; watch Aug/Sep revenue vs NT$26.8bn July run-rate, TrendForce 4Q26 print, and the TSMC WoW/CUBE deal as the AI-tier upgrade option.

dossier.business: Macronix is a Taiwanese integrated device manufacturer (own 12-inch fab, ~25,000 wafers/month) of non-volatile memory: NOR flash (48% of Q2 2026 revenue), SLC/MLC NAND and eMMC (43%), and mask ROM (largely Nintendo game cards). Customers are networking/telecom, automotive, industrial, consumer and, increasingly, AI-server/HPC OEMs that use high-density NOR for boot/firmware and eMMC/SLC NAND for BMC and local storage. It is the beneficiary of Samsung, Micron and SK Hynix exiting legacy 2D/MLC NAND and de-prioritising NOR as they chase HBM/3D NAND.
dossier.why_now: The bottleneck is real and more extreme than the working thesis states: TrendForce puts NOR flash contract prices up 100-120% in 1H26 alone (thesis says 15-80%), with further rises expected in 2H26 because no supplier has announced meaningful NOR/SLC NAND capacity additions. Macronix moved to monthly repricing in April 2026, its chairman said in July the fab would be fully loaded through H2, and management said AI servers have more than doubled demand for high-density (55nm) NOR. The result is a SanDisk-style earnings explosion: gross margin went 15.6% (Q2 2025) to 40.8% (Q1 2026) to 64.4% (Q2 2026), and a ten-quarter loss streak flipped to NT$7.7bn quarterly net income. However, the incremental driver in Q2 was actually NAND/eMMC (eMMC +317% QoQ, NAND share 30% to 43%), not NOR, and the market has already partially de-rated the stock (-37% from the June 23 high) on GigaDevice's "prices at historical highs" warning (Jul 1), a domestic broker target cut from NT$300 to NT$218 (Jul 29) citing flat eMMC spot prices, Morgan Stanley cutting its bear case to NT$100 (Aug 18), and a rates-driven memory selloff. The question is whether H2 pricing and Q3 EPS (needs to be >NT$4.5 to keep the "each quarter better" narrative) can re-anchor the multiple before 2027 capacity additions arrive.
dossier.analogue: Closest to the bottleneck plays (SanDisk/Micron): sold-out input, price up 100%+, earnings from loss to NT$7.7bn/quarter, gross margin 15.6% to 64.4% in four quarters. The fit on fundamentals is close, but the stock-path fit is worse: the market already gave the re-rating (NT$40 to NT$192, roughly 4.8x in six months) and has since taken a third of it back, whereas SanDisk/Micron in 2026 were still re-rating on each print. Macronix is a smaller, legacy-node, single-fab version of the trade with a 2027 capacity-response risk that the DRAM/HBM names did not face as acutely. Not a Dell (multiple is not low on trailing, ~29x TTM), not a Moderna binary, not an Intel turnaround.

dossier.bull_case: Fab fully loaded through H2 with monthly repricing on NOR and SLC NAND, so Q3 revenue rises to NT$22-24bn (July alone was NT$7.7bn) and gross margin moves toward the 70%+ management calls reachable, giving Q3 EPS of NT$4.5-5.5 and FY2026 EPS of NT$14-16. If Samsung/Micron/Hynix stay out of legacy NAND and NOR (TrendForce sees no NOR capacity additions announced) and AI-server high-density NOR plus eMMC keep growing, 2027 EPS can hold at NT$15+ even with some price normalisation; at 10-12x that is NT$150-180, in line with the NT$185-220 base targets from consensus and Morgan Stanley, i.e. 25-80% upside from NT$121.5. Net cash is building (Q2 FCF NT$7.4bn on a ~NT$6.5bn net-debt starting position), so the NT$37.8bn capex is self-funded and 3D NOR/3D NAND give a 2028 volume story.
dossier.bear_case: This is a peak-cycle legacy-node play: the incremental Q2 driver was NAND/eMMC, where a domestic broker already flagged flat eMMC spot prices, downgrades by TV/STB customers, module makers (Phison etc.) holding MLC inventory and SanDisk long-term pricing capping spot. TrendForce says Q3 NAND contract price growth slows to 10-15% QoQ with consumer demand weak and 2027 NAND supply exceeds demand; GigaDevice warned its NOR prices are at historical highs; CXMT's listing and Chinese legacy capacity add supply. Macronix's own +4-5k wpm arrives in 1H27 exactly as prices roll over, so 2027 EPS could fall to NT$6-8; at the 6-8x trough multiple memory names get at peak, that is NT$50-65, close to the Morgan Stanley bear case of NT$100 or below it. Foreign investors have been net sellers for weeks, and the stock has already shown it can lose 10% in a day on sector news.
dossier.what_confirms: August revenue above NT$8bn (>+4% MoM) and a Q3 2026 gross margin at or above 66% with EPS above NT$4.5 reported in late October, together with TrendForce confirming NOR/SLC NAND contract prices still rising QoQ in Q4 2026.
dossier.what_kills: A monthly revenue print that falls MoM before Q3 ends, or a Q3 gross margin below 60%, or any TrendForce/GigaDevice/Winbond datapoint showing NOR or SLC NAND contract prices flat-to-down QoQ in Q4 2026; equally, a major (Samsung/Micron) reversing its exit from legacy NAND or NOR.

dossier.business: Nanya Technology (Formosa Plastics Group) is Taiwan's largest DRAM maker, producing commodity DDR4, LPDDR4, DDR3 and a small (~10% of revenue) DDR5 line on its own 20nm/1x-class process at Fab 3 in New Taipei. DDR4 is 60-70% of revenue; customers are PC/consumer OEMs, module houses, networking (Cisco), SSD/controller vendors (SanDisk, Kioxia, Solidigm now hold equity and 3-year supply deals), industrial and automotive. It has no HBM and is not a credible HBM entrant; its whole 2026 story is being the marginal supplier of legacy DRAM that the big three (Samsung, SK hynix, Micron) are abandoning.
dossier.why_now: The bottleneck is legacy DRAM wafers. Micron issued DDR4/LPDDR4 EOL notices with final shipments in Q1 2026; Samsung and SK hynix delayed their DDR4 phase-outs only to end-2026 and are pushing wafers to HBM (which consumes ~3x the wafers per bit) and DDR5. CXMT halted legacy DRAM and is pivoting to DDR5/LPDDR5. That left Nanya (and Winbond) as the price-setters for DDR4: TrendForce reports DRAM contract prices rose ~90% QoQ in 1Q26, Nanya's own ASP rose >70% QoQ in Q1 and >60% in Q2 with flat bit shipments, and consumer-DRAM shortages have spilled over to DDR3 and even DDR2. Nanya's gross margin went from negative in 2024-25 to 79.5% in Q2 2026, net income from a loss to NT$50bn in a single quarter, and monthly revenue has set nine consecutive records (August NT$44.7bn, +561% YoY). Management says shortage lasts through end-2027, worst in 1H27; customers are prepaying and signing 3-year contracts; brokers say the October contract round could lift Q4 ASP another ~40%. TrendForce expects Q3 contract prices +13-18% (PC DRAM +15-20%) with gains "converging" in 4Q26 but not reversing, given 2027 supply tightness.
dossier.analogue: Bottleneck play: closest to Micron/SanDisk in the 2026 framework, and arguably a purer version. Sold-out input (DDR4 wafers), price spike (ASP roughly 3-4x in twelve months), earnings up far more than 7-21x (2025 EPS NT$2.13 vs. H1 2026 EPS NT$23.38 and a 2026 run-rate of NT$60-85), and the stock up ~10x in 12 months. Where it differs: the multiple has NOT re-rated (trailing P/E ~19x on a rapidly rising base, forward ~6-9x), i.e. the market treats it as a cyclical peak rather than a structural winner, and unlike Micron it has no HBM/DDR5 leg to carry it past the DDR4 cycle. Resemblance to the Micron/SanDisk template: high (about 8/10); it is the 'legacy tail' of the same bottleneck. It does not resemble the Dell (volume/low multiple), Moderna (binary) or Intel (government) analogues.

dossier.bull_case: DDR4 is a shrinking pie with only two non-Chinese producers left and demand that cannot migrate quickly (embedded, networking, automotive, older servers, SSD DRAM caches). Micron is out, Samsung/hynix stop at end-2026, CXMT has left legacy, and HBM4 wafer consumption keeps the majors' capacity locked up. Nanya's Q3 revenue tracks ~NT$130bn (+60% QoQ) at 80%+ gross margin, so Q3 EPS ~NT$25-27 and, with a +30-40% October contract reset, Q4 EPS NT$30-35: 2026 EPS ~NT$80-85, 2027 EPS NT$120+ if prices merely hold and bits grow modestly. At NT$496 that is ~6x 2026E and ~4x 2027E with NT$198bn net cash and customers prepaying under 3-year contracts. If the market accepts even a 10x multiple on 2027E, the stock is NT$1,000+, consistent with the most bullish Taiwan broker targets and above JPMorgan's NT$850. Kioxia, SanDisk, Solidigm and Cisco paying NT$223.9/share for 10% in March signals strategic buyers believed in duration when the stock was at half today's price.
dossier.bear_case: This is a peak-cycle commodity earnings print on a company that lost money for 11 consecutive quarters through mid-2025 and whose bit shipments are flat: 100% of growth is price. TrendForce already says 4Q26 increases will 'converge' as consumer demand weakens and inventory builds; DDR4 spot has periodically slipped (April 2026 spot -1.2%). Samsung and SK hynix kept DDR4 lines running precisely because it became a 'cash cow', and every quarter of NT$50bn profit at Nanya is an invitation for them to extend again or for CXMT to re-enter (CXMT reaches ~350k WSPM by end-2026, close to Micron). The August tape already shows the market front-running the peak: -7.8% on record revenue, MSCI inclusion at the top, three circuit-breaker moves in six months. Meanwhile Nanya is about to spend NT$346bn on Fab 5A through 2029 (capex ~NT$200bn in 2027 vs. NT$13bn in 2025), i.e. it will consume its cash pile building 10nm-class capacity that arrives in 2028, exactly when the cycle has historically turned; at that point earnings can fall 80%+ in four quarters, as they did in 2022-23. If 2027 EPS is NT$40 instead of NT$120 and the trough multiple is 10x, the stock is NT$400 or lower, and at a normalised mid-cycle EPS of NT$15-20 it is NT$200-250.
dossier.what_confirms: The October contract round producing a Q4 DDR4 contract price increase of 25%+ QoQ (brokers' +40% claim), September revenue at or above NT$46bn taking Q3 to NT$135bn+, and management at the ~mid-October call re-affirming shortage through 2027 with named long-term contracts covering 2027 volumes; plus Samsung confirming DDR4 exit by end-2026 rather than another extension.
dossier.what_kills: A flat-to-down Q4 DDR4 contract price (TrendForce 4Q26 consumer DRAM at 0% or negative), a monthly revenue print that falls MoM while Nanya is capacity-constrained (would mean price, not volume, is rolling), Samsung/SK hynix announcing another DDR4 extension into 2027 or CXMT restarting DDR4 for export, or any Q3 gross margin decline from 79.5% while ASP is still supposedly rising.

Cumulative Fab 5A spend roughly equals current net cash plus ~1.5 years of peak earnings, so a downturn in 2027-28 would push Nanya back to the debt/rights-issue profile it had in 2023 (it did a rights issue then). Dilution risk near term: low (placement done, earnings cover capex at current prices); medium term: meaningful if DRAM prices normalise before 5A is funded. skeptic.evidence_quality: Caveat first: I could not run independent web checks (search quota exhausted, fetches blocked), so this is an internal-consistency and cross-dossier review, not fresh verification. On that basis the dossier holds up well: the revenue chain (Q1 NT$49.09bn, Q2 NT$82.55bn = +68.2%, July NT$43.87bn = +49.3% MoM on an implied June of NT$29.4bn, August NT$44.69bn = +1.9% MoM, Jan-Aug NT$220.2bn) sums exactly; EPS, share count, placement size (351.57m x NT$223.9 = NT$78.72bn), market cap, EV/sales and P/E all reconcile; the TrendForce 3Q26 +13-18% figure and the Nanya/Winbond as residual DDR4 suppliers framing are corroborated by the Winbond dossier. Weaknesses: primary sources (Nanya IR, TrendForce) were unreachable for the analyst too, so nearly everything is from Taiwanese financial press and aggregators (CMoney, BigGo, UDN, Statementdog); the 52-week high is internally contradictory (NT$505/511/530/569); the 'Q4 ASP +40%' and 'Jul+Aug = 72% of Q3' claims are broker chatter relayed second-hand; all published consensus EPS figures are stale, so the valuation rests on the analyst's own run-rate arithmetic; short interest, YTD return, Q3 results date and exact share count are unconfirmed, and the analyst honestly lists all of this. The sibling dossier's statement that Samsung/SK hynix extended DDR4 into 2027 directly conflicts with this dossier's end-2026 assumption and needs resolving before sizing.
corrections: 12-month move: NT$42.10 low to NT$496 is ~11.8x, not 'roughly 10-11x'; StockAnalysis's +1,058% at NT$521 implies a base of ~NT$45, i.e. ~11x at NT$496. Say '11-12x from the 52-week low'.

H1 2026 EPS of NT$23.38 is the period-weighted figure (H1 net income NT$76.25bn / ~3.26bn weighted shares); the sum of the quarterly EPS is 8.41 + 14.66 = NT$23.07, and on the current ~3.45bn share count H1 EPS is ~NT$22.1. Forward EPS (Q3E NT$25+, 2026E NT$75-90) should be computed on 3.45-3.5bn shares, not on H1 weighted shares.

Share count: 351.57m placement shares = 10.19% of enlarged capital implies ~3.45bn shares, while Statementdog's NT$1,605bn at NT$457 implies ~3.51bn. Market cap at NT$496 is therefore NT$1.71-1.74tn; state the range rather than a point.

2026E EPS of 'NT$75-90': the NT$90 top requires ~NT$310bn net income, i.e. ~73% net margin on ~NT$425bn revenue, versus 60.8% net margin in Q2. NT$75-85 is the defensible range; NT$90 needs the +40% Q4 reset to land in full.

'Jul+Aug already equal 72% of one broker's Q3 estimate' implies that broker's Q3 estimate is ~NT$123bn (+49% QoQ); against Morgan Stanley's +60% QoQ (~NT$132bn, the figure used in the catalysts table) Jul+Aug is 67%. Label which estimate is being used.
what_confirms threshold: September revenue of NT$46bn gives Q3 = 88.56 + 46 = NT$134.6bn, not 'NT$135bn+'; the threshold should be ~NT$46.5bn.

Supplier-exit timeline conflicts with the team's own Winbond dossier, which states Samsung and SK hynix have extended DDR4 production into 2026-27 and SK hynix is boosting DDR4 output at Wuxi; this dossier says phase-outs end-2026 and treats a further extension as a December 2026 catalyst. One of the two is wrong and it is the single most important durability fact.

Missing datapoint: DDR4 8Gb contract at a record US$25 in Aug 2026 (cited in the Winbond dossier) implies >10x the mid-2025 price, versus Nanya's realised ASP of ~3-4x; the gap (LTA pricing, mix, lag) should be stated because it both caps the October-reset upside on LTA volumes and means DDR4 is now priced well above DDR5 per bit, the main driver of demand migration.

Loss streak: '11 consecutive quarters of losses through Q2 2025' vs. '2025 EPS NT$2.13' and '2H25 EPS NT$2.39' implies 1H25 EPS of about -0.26 and leaves Q3 2025 ambiguous; if Q3 2025 was also a loss the streak is 12 quarters. Verify before quoting.

input.thesis: OSAT absorbing CoWoS advanced-packaging overflow from TSMC, with a $7B Arizona packaging plant under a TSMC MoU; packaging is the AI bottleneck with lead times over 12 months.

dossier.name: Amkor Technology, Inc.
dossier.market_cap: ~$11.6B at $46.82 (Sept 3, 2026 close, per Robinhood/StockAnalysis snippet)
dossier.business: Amkor is the largest US-headquartered OSAT (outsourced semiconductor assembly and test): it takes finished wafers from foundries (mainly TSMC) and packages and tests them into chips for fabless and IDM customers, with factories in Korea, Taiwan, Japan, Philippines, Vietnam, Portugal and a campus under construction in Peoria, Arizona. Revenue ($6.7B in 2025) splits across Communications (premium smartphones, largely the iOS ecosystem), Computing (data-center AI/HPC, CPUs, PCs), Automotive & Industrial, and Consumer. Growth is now driven by advanced packaging platforms, 2.5D (CoWoS-class) and high-density fan-out (HDFO), which management said would roughly triple in revenue in 2026.
dossier.why_now: The bottleneck is TSMC CoWoS/advanced-packaging capacity, reported sold out through 2026 with new lines taking 12-18 months to qualify; TSMC has been handing a slice of the CoWoS back-end (reported 240-270k wafers/yr in 2026, of which Amkor ~180-190k, per a low-reliability substack/BigGo estimate) to ASE/SPIL and Amkor. Evidence that the bottleneck is biting on price: ASE reportedly raised advanced-packaging quotes by more than 20% in July 2026 (TrendForce) and OSAT utilization is cited near 90%. Amkor's Computing segment hit a record in Q2 2026 (+20% q/q) and is guided up ~30% q/q in Q3 on AI data-center demand plus an HDFO CPU ramp; gross margin expanded 480bps y/y to 16.8% and is guided to 18.5-19.5% in Q3. Layered on top are two anchor contracts signed in the last 90 days: a 10-year TSMC Arizona packaging agreement (June 16-17, 2026, upgrading the Oct-2024 MoU) and a $1.5B Nvidia prepayment (July 23, 2026) to fund US capacity. The tension: the stock has already round-tripped from a $96.68 high (June 2026) to ~$47 after a Q3 guide ($1.95-2.05B) that missed the ~$2.12B consensus, because a SiP migration from Korea to Vietnam and Android memory constraints are dragging Communications down high-single-digits q/q, with disruption flagged through Q4 2026 into H1 2027.
dossier.analogue: Closest to the Dell analogue (volume beneficiary on a modest multiple) with a bottleneck kicker, not a Micron/SanDisk analogue. Similarities to the bottleneck plays: the input (advanced-packaging capacity) is sold out, peers are raising prices 20%+, and Amkor's EPS is compounding fast (Q2 net income +219% y/y; 2026 consensus EPS ~$2.55-2.60 vs $1.50 in 2025, i.e. ~1.7x, not 7-21x). Differences that matter: Amkor is the overflow supplier, not the scarce asset owner, so it gets volume rather than a price spike (gross margin 17-19%, vs memory names moving to 50%+); its Communications book (iPhone SiP) is a cyclical anchor that just caused a 23-25% one-day drop; and it is spending $2.5-3.0B of capex (~40% of revenue) with negative FCF, so the earnings leverage arrives in 2027-2030, not in the next two prints. There is also a minor Intel-style government-backed-buildout element (up to $400M CHIPS Act award, Nvidia prepay, TSMC 10-year deal). Net: 'Dell with an Arizona option', maybe 60% fit to the volume-beneficiary bucket and 25% to the bottleneck bucket.

dossier.guidance: Q3 2026 (given July 27, 2026): revenue $1.95-2.05B (consensus was ~$2.11-2.12B), gross margin 18.5-19.5%, net income $180-205M, EPS $0.72-0.82. Investor Day (May 21, 2026) long-term model: revenue $9.0B +/- $0.5B in 2028 (from $6.7B in 2025) with gross margin 17.5% +/- 100bps; ~$11B+ revenue and ~22%+ gross margin by 2030; Arizona phase 1 to contribute ~$1B revenue at >30% gross margin by 2030, with production start cited as 2027 at Investor Day but 'early 2028' in the Oct-2025 groundbreaking coverage. Trailing P/E on my derived TTM EPS of roughly $2.2 (FY25 $1.50 less Q1/Q2-2025 plus Q1/Q2-2026; approximate) is ~21x. EV/sales on ~$7.6B 2026 run-rate revenue with roughly net-zero cash is ~1.5x. Versus history: Amkor traded ~10-15x through 2022-2024 as a low-growth OSAT, so ~18x is a re-rating but a modest one for 25%+ growth. Versus peers: a Zacks piece (mid-2026) had ASE at 19x 2026 P/E vs Amkor 28x; after the July collapse Amkor is now roughly in line with ASE. Price/FCF is meaningless (FCF negative in 2026). Verdict: the multiple embeds the 2026 growth and margin recovery but not the 2028-2030 Investor Day model ($9B/17.5% GM -> ~$3.3-3.8 EPS if achieved; $11B/22% GM implies well over $5); the Arizona/CoWoS-overflow thesis is priced as an option, not a certainty. Caveat: 2027 consensus EPS not found, and the convertible ($106.37 conversion price, capped call) is far out of the money so no near-term dilution in the multiple.

dossier.bull_case: TSMC's CoWoS remains sold out through 2026 and outsourcing to OSATs rises with each Nvidia generation; Amkor is the only non-Taiwanese OSAT with a TSMC 10-year agreement, a $1.5B Nvidia prepayment, Apple as an anchor Arizona customer and up to $400M of CHIPS money. If the Q3 guide holds ($2.0B, 19% GM, ~$0.77 EPS) and Q4 is similar, 2026 EPS lands ~$2.6-2.7 and 2027 could reach $3.5+ as Computing (guided +30% q/q) keeps compounding, 2.5D/HDFO triples, Vietnam absorbs low-end SiP, and Korea's premium cleanroom fills with AI programs. A return to the 25x forward multiple the stock carried in June on $3.5 of 2027 EPS is ~$85-90 (+80-90%). The 2030 model ($11B revenue, 22%+ GM, Arizona $1B at >30% GM) would imply EPS north of $5, making today's price under 10x that outcome. ASE's 20%+ advanced-packaging price hikes suggest Amkor also has pricing power it has not yet shown in margins.
dossier.bear_case: Amkor is the overflow valve, not the bottleneck owner: TSMC is adding CoWoS capacity to 120-140k wafers/month by end-2026 (from ~70k), and as TSMC's own AP lines and Arizona AP fabs come up the outsourced slice can shrink, leaving Amkor with $2.5-3.0B/yr of capex (~40% of sales), negative FCF (-$307M in H1 2026), $2.5B of debt and a gross margin still below 20%. The July 28 collapse (-23 to -25% in a day) showed how exposed earnings are to the iPhone SiP book: a high-single-digit q/q Communications decline was enough to take Q3 revenue $70-170M below consensus, and management says the Vietnam migration drag lasts into H1 2027. If Q3 gross margin misses the 18.5% floor or Q4 is guided flat, 2026 EPS slips toward $2.3 and the stock at 15x (ASE-like) is ~$35 (-25%). Longer term, if Arizona's phase-1 production slips from 2027 to 2028 (the groundbreaking coverage already says early 2028) or Apple/Nvidia volumes underfill it, the >30% GM promise evaporates and the $1.0B convert plus 2033 notes weigh on a company whose 2025 EPS was only $1.50.
dossier.what_confirms: Q3 2026 print showing Computing up ~30% q/q with total revenue at or above $2.0B and gross margin at or above 19%, plus a Q4 guide that keeps gross margin above 19% and implies 2026 EPS above $2.60; and, separately, any TSMC/Nvidia/DigiTimes datapoint that the 2027 outsourced CoWoS allocation to Amkor rises versus the reported ~180-190k wafers for 2026.
dossier.what_kills: Q3 gross margin below 18.5% or Q4 revenue guided below ~$2.0B (i.e. Computing failing to offset Communications), or reports that TSMC is pulling CoWoS volume back in-house / to SPIL as its 120-140k wafers/month capacity lands, or an Arizona phase-1 production slip beyond 2028 / a CHIPS award or Nvidia prepay renegotiation.

Debt includes 5.875% senior notes due 2033 and $1.0B of 0% convertible senior notes due 2031 issued May 2026 (conversion price ~$106.37, 52.5% premium at issue; capped call purchased, so dilution risk is nil below the cap and modest above ~$106; $150M greenshoe may have lifted the total to $1.15B). Cash burn: H1 2026 FCF about -$307M (OCF $381.5M vs capex $688.4M) with FY2026 capex guided $2.5-3.0B, implying ~$2B of H2 capex and a likely FY2026 FCF of roughly -$1B before the Nvidia $1.5B prepayment and CHIPS disbursements (timing of both not disclosed). Dividend ($0.0835/qtr, ~$83M/yr) and $300M buyback authorization are small relative to capex. Dilution risk: low near term; refinancing risk: low given liquidity, but leverage rises through 2027 if capex stays elevated.
dossier.suggested_sizing: Sleeve 1-1.5% for a risk-aware investor (not core): the stock just proved it can drop 25% in a day on a non-AI segment, FCF is negative through at least 2027, and the Arizona economics are unproven until 2028. Scale toward 2-2.5% only if the Q3 print confirms 19%+ gross margin with Computing at the guided +30% q/q; treat any add above that as conditional on 2027 capex stepping down.

skeptic.priced_in: Partly. The pure bottleneck narrative was fully priced at $93-97 in June (28x+ forward) and has been half-unwound to ~$47 (~18x 2026 consensus EPS of $2.55-2.60, ~1.5x EV/sales) by a Communications/iPhone-SiP air pocket that is unrelated to AI packaging. That is a sensible entry setup, but two things temper it: (1) consensus already embeds ~70% EPS growth in 2026, so the print has to keep delivering 19%+ gross margin just to hold the multiple; and (2) the market is no longer paying for the 2028-2030 Investor Day model (Arizona >30% GM, $11B revenue) partly because FCF is negative through 2027 and the July 28 collapse showed that a high-single-digit q/q move in the phone book can swamp a +30% q/q Computing ramp. Note the stock is still ~+90-100% off its Sept-2025 low, so 'mid' rather than 'early' is right; the dossier's own '+65% 12-month' figure understates this because it uses a Sept 19 base rather than the early-Sept low.
skeptic.durability: The bottleneck is real but Amkor is the overflow valve, not the owner of the scarce asset, and the dossier is correctly honest about that. Durability hinges on TSMC continuing to outsource CoWoS back-end even as its own capacity goes from ~70k to 120-140k wafers/month by end-2026 and as TSMC's own Arizona advanced-packaging fabs come up; if TSMC pulls work in-house or favours SPIL, Amkor is left with $2.5-3.0B/yr of capex and sub-20% gross margins. The reported 2026 allocation (Amkor ~180-190k wafers/yr vs SPIL 60-80k) comes from a substack/BigGo summary and is counter-intuitive given SPIL's historical primacy in CoWoS-oS, so I would not underwrite it. Positives for durability: a 10-year TSMC Arizona agreement (not just the MoU the working thesis cites), a $1.5B Nvidia prepayment, Apple as an Arizona anchor, and ASE's 20%+ price hikes signalling tight OSAT utilisation. Gaps the dossier does not address: substrate/T-glass and HBM supply constraints that could cap Amkor's output regardless of demand, competing capacity from Intel Foundry (EMIB/Foveros) and Samsung (I-Cube) being pitched to hyperscalers, panel-level/CoPoS transitions that could strand 2.5D tooling, tariff/Section 232 exposure for a company with most capacity in Korea/Taiwan/Vietnam, and Apple customer concentration (historically >20% of sales) which is the actual source of the recent volatility.
skeptic.evidence_quality: Mixed, and I could not independently test any of it today: the session's web-search budget was exhausted (200/200) before my queries ran and every WebFetch (stockanalysis, ir.amkor.com, TrendForce, DigiTimes) was egress-blocked, so this review is an internal-consistency audit of the dossier plus my own recall, not fresh verification. The dossier's core P&L figures (Q2 $1.90B, 16.8% GM, $174M/$0.70, Q3 guide $1.95-2.05B / 18.5-19.5% GM / $0.72-0.82) are internally consistent with a ~248M share count, the dividend, short interest and market cap, and are anchored to an Amkor IR PDF, an 8-K summary and BusinessWire. Weak links the analyst already flags and I agree are weak: H1 cash flow from an X post, the CoWoS outsourcing split from a substack, cash/debt from Quartr snippets, consensus EPS from Simply Wall St/Benzinga of unknown date, and no 2027 consensus. One number looks wrong on its face (the '+219% y/y' Q2 net income growth) and the TTM EPS arithmetic is slightly off; see corrections. Overall the dossier is well-hedged and candid, but the thesis-critical inputs (outsourced CoWoS volume to Amkor, Arizona timing, FCF path) are the least well-sourced.
corrections: Working thesis says the Arizona plant is 'under a TSMC MoU': per the dossier's own sources (ir.amkor.com, pr.tsmc.com/english/news/3174, TrendForce 2026-06-17) the Oct-2024 MoU was upgraded to a 10-year definitive TSMC-Amkor Arizona agreement in June 2026. Also '$7B' is the total campus commitment; phase 1 is ~$2B and is what produces in 2027-28.

Analogue section: 'Q2 net income +219% y/y' does not reconcile. Q2 2025 net income was ~$18M ($0.07 EPS) on $1.51B revenue (consistent with the dossier's +26% revenue growth and 12.0% prior-year GM), so $174M is roughly 9-10x, not +219%. Verify the base; the 219% may be a mis-copied EPS or operating-income comparison.

Valuation: derived TTM EPS '~$2.2' should be ~$2.37 (FY25 $1.50 - Q1'25 $0.09 - Q2'25 $0.07 + Q1'26 $0.33 + Q2'26 $0.70), giving a trailing P/E of ~20x rather than ~21x. Immaterial to the verdict but the arithmetic is off.

Price action: '12-month move roughly +65%' is measured from the Sept 19, 2025 close ($28.31). Against the actual one-year-ago price (Sept 2-3, 2025, ~$23.4-24.6, the 52-week low) the move is ~+90-100%, which the dossier's own '~90% above the 52-week low' line already implies.

Capex '~40% of revenue': $2.5-3.0B on the dossier's own ~$7.6B 2026 run-rate is 33-39% (midpoint ~36%). Also worth flagging that H1 capex of $688M vs a $2.5-3.0B full-year guide implies $1.8-2.3B in H2, a 3x step-up; either the guide is front-loaded optimism or the H1 figure (from an X post) is wrong.

Working thesis claim 'lead times over 12 months' conflates two things: the dossier sources 12-18 months to qualify new CoWoS lines (capacity-add lead time), not customer order lead times. No source in the dossier gives a customer-facing lead time for Amkor's 2.5D/HDFO services.
skeptic.one_line: AMKR ~$47 (~18x 2026E, 52% off June high): TSMC CoWoS overflow + 10-yr TSMC Arizona deal + $1.5B Nvidia prepay, but negative FCF through 2027 and an iPhone-SiP air pocket into H1'27; needs Q3 (late Oct/early Nov) to show 19%+ GM and Computing +30% q/q before sizing above 1-1.5%.

dossier.market_cap: ~US$82-83B (stockanalysis.com showed US$83.48B on 17-Jul-2026; at the 3-Sep-2026 ADR price of ~US$37.5 and ~4.39B common shares implied by Q2 EPS, roughly US$82B)
dossier.business: ASE is the world's largest outsourced semiconductor assembly and test (OSAT) provider: its ATM segment (Assembly, Test and Materials; ~66% of Q2-26 revenue, NT$126.1B) packages and tests chips for fabless and IDM customers (NVIDIA, AMD, Broadcom, Marvell, Qualcomm, MediaTek, Apple supply chain), and its EMS segment (USI; ~34%) does low-margin electronics manufacturing. The growth engine is "LEAP" (Leading-Edge Advanced Packaging: CoWoS-type 2.5D on-substrate work, FoCoS, panel-level fan-out and advanced test), which grew from ~US$0.6B (2024) to US$1.6B (2025) and is guided to ~US$3.7B in 2026, much of it as overflow/back-end steps outsourced by TSMC for AI accelerators.
dossier.why_now: The bottleneck is advanced packaging and test capacity, not wafers or end-demand. TSMC's CoWoS-S/-L lines are reported sold out through 2026 with lead times into 2027, and TSMC has pushed on-substrate (CoW-on-S) steps and some full-process packaging for NVIDIA Rubin and AMD Venice to ASE/SPIL and Amkor. On the 30-Jul-2026 Q2 call management said "the business demand is not a concern, it's our own capability to execute" and that "all of our customers are asking for more devices for Q3 and Q4"; Q3 ATM growth of 11-13% QoQ is explicitly capped by how much capacity can be installed. TrendForce reported on 1-Jul-2026 that ASE raised advanced-packaging quotes by more than 20% (CoWoS and FoCoS, major US customers affected). LEAP revenue has already blown through the US$3.5B 2026 target (~US$3.7B now), the 2027 target was lifted from US$5.5B to at least US$7.5B, and 2026 capex was raised twice to a record US$10.5B. The thesis "advanced packaging doubles in 2026" is therefore confirmed by company guidance (2.3x, US$1.6B to ~US$3.7B); the live question is whether the 2027 second doubling and a >30% ATM gross margin can be delivered while capex runs above EBITDA.
dossier.analogue: Closest to the bottleneck-play bucket (SanDisk/Micron/Seagate): sold-out capacity, 20%+ price hikes, customer over-ordering, multiple re-rated from low-teens to high-20s forward P/E. But the resemblance is partial, maybe 50-60%. Differences: (1) earnings are up ~2-3x, not 7-21x, because ASE is a service provider with a capex-heavy, depreciation-laden model and a 34% EMS mix at ~single-digit margins; (2) the "price spike" is a 20% quote increase, not a doubling of a commodity price; (3) ASE's scarcity is partly borrowed from TSMC, which controls how much overflow it hands out and is itself doubling CoWoS capacity (industry gap reportedly narrowing from ~20% to ~10% by end-2026). It also has a leg in the volume-beneficiary bucket (Dell-like: growth via more units at modest margin) but on a much higher multiple than Dell. Net: a capex-heavy, lower-torque cousin of the memory bottleneck trade whose multiple already reflects the bottleneck.

Versus its own history ASE was a low-to-mid-teens P/E commodity OSAT before 2025 (exact historical band not verified). The multiple has roughly doubled, so the 2026 doubling is fully embedded; the 2027 doubling is only partly in Street numbers (Zacks 2027 growth +36% vs company LEAP +100%), which is where any remaining upside sits. Analyst PTs cluster US$34-48 (Zacks avg ~US$34, Goldman Buy US$43 from 1-May-2026, Financhill US$46), i.e. consensus sees little upside from here.

dossier.how_far_run_note: The specific thesis as stated (advanced packaging doubling in 2026 on TSMC overflow) is late: it is in guidance, in the twice-raised capex, in a 300% 12-month move and in a forward multiple that has gone from low-teens to high-20s. The stock's negative reaction to a Q2 EPS beat, consensus targets at or near the price, and a 16% drawdown from the June high all say the 2026 leg is priced. What is only partly priced is the 2027 leg: LEAP >=US$7.5B (+100%) and Q4-26 ATM GM >30%, against Street 2027 EPS growth of ~36% (stale) and a bear camp (Seeking Alpha "fully priced in", "US$8.5B capex gamble") worried about depreciation and negative FCF. Hence "mid" overall: no longer early, not yet a busted trade, with returns now dependent on 2027 estimate revisions rather than the 2026 story.

dossier.bull_case: LEAP compounds from US$1.6B (2025) to ~US$3.7B (2026) to >=US$7.5B (2027) as TSMC keeps CoWoS-S/-L sold out and hands ASE more on-substrate and, from H2-26, full-process work; ATM revenue grows 35% in 2026 and ATM gross margin steps from 27.3% (Q2) to >30% in Q4 on mix and the 20%+ price hikes, lifting consolidated GM toward 23-24% in 2027. On that path 2027 ADS EPS of US$2.0-2.3 is reachable (vs stale consensus ~US$1.43); a 25x multiple on US$2.2 gives ~US$55, roughly 45% upside from US$37.5, and the stock re-tests and clears the US$44.67 June high once Q3/Q4 prints show the margin inflection. Balance sheet can carry it: net debt/equity 0.47, NT$396B undrawn lines, US$1B CB already placed, EBITDA run-rate ~US$6B. Panel-level packaging (FOPLP) and advanced test add optionality beyond CoWoS overflow.
dossier.bear_case: ASE is spending US$10.5B of capex against ~US$6B of annualised EBITDA, so free cash flow is negative by several billion dollars in 2026 and management says it stays negative "for some time"; interest-bearing debt rose NT$40.9B in one quarter to NT$306B and a US$1B zero-coupon CB adds dilution. Depreciation from 13 new fabs and 8 expansions lands before revenue, so the Q4 ">30% ATM GM" could slip and 2027 consolidated margins could stall around 21-22%. TSMC is doubling its own CoWoS capacity (industry gap reportedly shrinking from ~20% to ~10% by end-2026) and pushing CoPoS/exclusive next-gen flows, so the overflow ASE receives is at TSMC's discretion and could shrink in 2027-28, leaving ASE with over-built 2.5D capacity and a 20% price hike that reverses. Amkor trades at ~21x forward vs ASE ~28x; if 2027 LEAP lands at US$5.5-6B instead of US$7.5B and EPS at ~US$1.5, the stock de-rates to 18-20x and ~US$28-30 (20-25% downside). The stock already fell on a 45% EPS beat, and consensus targets (~US$34-48) offer little cushion.
dossier.what_confirms: Q3-26 (late Oct) ATM gross margin at or above 29% with Q4 guided >30%, September/Q3 monthly revenue confirming the +21-22% QoQ consolidated guide, and the 2027 LEAP target reiterated or raised above US$7.5B with full-process (AMD Venice) revenue tracking the US$300-400M 2026 estimate. A second-order confirmation: TSMC's Q3 call describing OSAT outsourcing as structural rather than temporary overflow.
dossier.what_kills: Q4-26 ATM gross margin guided below 28% (depreciation outrunning mix), any cut to the US$7.5B 2027 LEAP target or the US$10.5B capex plan, or TSMC/industry reports that CoWoS supply-demand has balanced and outsourcing to OSATs is being pulled back in 2027. A reversal of the 20% price hike or monthly ATM revenue growth falling below the 11-13% QoQ Q3 guide would be early warnings.
dossier.balance_sheet: 30-Jun-2026: cash NT$91.3B (~US$3.0B); interest-bearing debt NT$306.2B (~US$10B), up NT$40.9B in the quarter; net debt ~NT$215B (~US$7B); net debt/equity 0.47; current ratio 1.07; NT$396B undrawn credit lines; total assets >NT$1.07T. H1-26 investment outlays exceeded operating cash flow and were funded by NT$39.9B of net borrowing and bond proceeds; FY26 capex US$10.5B vs EBITDA run-rate ~US$6B implies roughly US$3-4B negative FCF this year, and management says it stays negative into 2027. Financing: US$1B zero-coupon currency-linked convertible bonds due 2031 (convertible into common shares, i.e. modest dilution of ~1-2% at conversion, exact conversion price not found) plus a 2026 first-series unsecured corporate bond approved by the board in April 2026. Dividend: US$0.36 per ADS paid in 2026 (ex-date 6-Jul-2026), ~1% yield. Not distressed, but the model is now capex-funded by leverage, so the equity is exposed if utilisation or pricing rolls over.
dossier.suggested_sizing: Sleeve 1-2% for a risk-aware investor at ~US$37-38: the 2026 doubling is priced, so entry return depends on 2027 estimate revisions and margin delivery. Scale toward a 3% core only on either (a) a Q3 print that confirms ATM GM >=29% and reiterates/raises the US$7.5B 2027 LEAP target, or (b) a pullback toward ~20x forward (roughly US$28-30). Not a lottery-ticket name; the balance sheet and TSMC dependency argue against sizing it like the memory bottleneck plays.

skeptic.priced_in: Largely yes for the thesis as written. The dossier's own tape says it: ADR +~300% over 12 months (US$9.52 low to ~US$37.5), forward P/E re-rated from low-teens to ~28x versus Amkor ~21x, the stock fell on a 45% Q2 EPS beat, it sits ~16% below the 30-Jun high and has been range-bound US$35-40 for five weeks, and sell-side targets (US$34-48, Zacks average ~US$34) straddle the current price. The 2026 LEAP doubling (US$1.6B to ~US$3.7B, i.e. 2.3x) is in company guidance, in a twice-raised capex budget and in a 20%+ price hike already reported by TrendForce, so nobody buying today is paying for the 2026 story. The residual argument is that Street 2027 EPS (Zacks ~US$1.43, +36%) is stale against management's >=US$7.5B 2027 LEAP target; the dossier's own derivation of 2027 EPS US$2.0-2.3 would put the stock at <20x, which is the only place upside lives. That is an estimate-revision trade, not a discovery trade, and it depends on Q3/Q4 margin prints that management has already telegraphed.
skeptic.durability: Weaker than the memory-bottleneck analogues the dossier compares it to, and the dossier is honest about this. ASE's scarcity is borrowed: TSMC decides how much CoW-on-S and full-process work to hand out, is doubling its own CoWoS capacity, and the dossier cites a TrendForce report of the industry supply-demand gap narrowing from ~20% to ~10% by end-2026. Once TSMC's own lines catch up, the 20%+ quote increases are the first thing to reverse. Meanwhile ASE is committing US$10.5B of capex against ~US$6B annualised EBITDA, funded by NT$40.9B of new borrowing in a single quarter plus a US$1B CB, with management explicitly guiding negative FCF 'for some time' and depreciation landing before revenue from 13 new fabs and 8 expansions. Two offsets: full-process packaging (AMD Venice, NVIDIA Rubin) is stickier than pure overflow, and CoWoS-L/SoIC complexity gives TSMC reasons to keep back-end steps outsourced. Net: the bottleneck looks durable through mid-2027 but is TSMC-discretionary beyond that, and the equity carries the capex risk if utilisation or pricing rolls over in 2027-28.
skeptic.evidence_quality: Important caveat: I could not run any independent check. The session's WebSearch budget was exhausted (200/200) before this review, curl was blocked at the proxy (403 CONNECT), and WebFetch returned EGRESS_BLOCKED for ir.aseglobal.com, prnewswire.com and trendforce.com. Everything below is a desk audit of the dossier's internal arithmetic. On that basis the dossier hangs together well: share count implied by NI/EPS (NT$21,068M / NT$4.80 = 4.39B) reconciles to the ~US$82B market cap at US$37.5 per ADS (2 shares/ADS); ATM at NT$126.1B is exactly 66% of NT$191.1B; the Q3 guide reconciles (ATM +12% and EMS +40% give consolidated +21.5%); the trailing P/E of ~45x reconciles to roughly US$0.80 of trailing ADS EPS; 3711.TW at NT$588 vs the ADR at US$37.5 implies ~31.4 TWD/USD, which is plausible. The dossier itself admits both WebFetch attempts on primary documents were blocked and that all figures come from search snippets, the short-interest figure is eight months stale, the 2027 EPS is the analyst's own derivation, and the CB conversion price was not found. Treat all headline numbers as plausible-but-unverified secondary-source figures; the orchestrator should re-run verification (Q2 press release, TrendForce 31-Jul piece, August monthly revenue due ~10-Sep) when search budget is available.
corrections: Earnings quality not flagged: Q2 net income NT$21,068M is essentially equal to operating profit NT$21,134M and grew +180% YoY versus operating profit +107%. With ~NT$306B of interest-bearing debt and Taiwanese tax, that gap implies sizeable non-operating income (FX/investment gains) in Q2; the '45% EPS beat' and the US$0.29 ADS EPS base used for the 2026 US$1.30-1.45 derivation may be partly non-recurring. The dossier should decompose this before extrapolating.

Capex phasing not flagged: H1-26 spend was ~US$4.1B against a US$10.5B full-year budget, which implies ~US$6.4B in H2, a ~56% step-up on H1's run-rate. Either the budget slips into 2027 (better near-term FCF, worse 2027 depreciation) or 2H depreciation ramps harder than the '>30% ATM GM in Q4' guide assumes. The bear/bull cases should state which they assume.

Q3 revenue math: July NT$73.8B is ~16% above the Q2 monthly average (NT$63.7B), but hitting the +21-22% QoQ consolidated guide (~NT$232B) requires August and September to average ~NT$79B, i.e. continued MoM growth, not a plateau. The 'watch August' catalyst should carry that explicit hurdle (~NT$76-80B) rather than only the YoY figure.

Minor inconsistency: '+300% over 12 months' (price) and 'market cap +274% in one year' are both quoted without reconciling; the difference implies either share-count changes or different measurement windows. Not material, but pick one.

Trailing P/E range '45x to 60x+': the dossier's own numbers (Q1 ~US$0.21, Q2 US$0.29 per ADS, plus two ~US$0.15 quarters) give ~US$0.80 trailing EPS and ~47x; the 60x+ figures from Seeking Alpha/Simply Wall St are almost certainly using pre-Q2 trailing EPS and should be labelled stale rather than presented as a range.

Working-thesis wording: 'advanced packaging sales expected to double in 2026' understates company guidance, which is ~2.3x (US$1.6B to ~US$3.7B); more importantly the doubling is already in guidance since 30-Jul-2026, so it is a confirmed fact, not an expectation, and should be described as such on the watchlist.

Sleeve size; add on Q3 (late Oct) margin proof or a pullback to ~US$28-30. Note: no independent verification possible this session.

input.name: Hammond Power Solutions
input.thesis: Dry-type transformer maker with roughly 23 percent share, backlog up 97 percent YoY, Q2 2026 sales up 45 percent, in a market where transformer lead times are 3 to 5 years and half of US data-center builds are delayed by electrical gear.

dossier.name: Hammond Power Solutions Inc.
dossier.market_cap: ~C$2.9B at C$242.12 (Sept 4, 2026 close) on ~11.9M total Class A + Class B shares; EV roughly C$3.2-3.3B including the post-AEG debt (estimate, see balance_sheet)
dossier.business: Guelph, Ontario-based designer and manufacturer of dry-type (air-cooled) low- and medium-voltage transformers, cast-resin units, custom magnetics and power-quality gear, plus a smaller liquid-filled distribution transformer line, sold through electrical distributors, OEMs and private-label channels in the US (the majority of sales), Canada, Mexico and India. Marketed as the largest dry-type transformer maker in North America; end markets are commercial construction, industrial electrification, utilities, renewables/EV charging and, increasingly, data centres (now over 30% of revenue). On June 29, 2026 it closed the C$365M all-cash acquisition of AEG Power Solutions, a European/Asian industrial power-electronics maker with ~C$326M of 2025 revenue and five plants.
dossier.why_now: The bottleneck is electrical gear for the AI build-out: Bloomberg-sourced reporting says only ~4 GW of the ~12 GW of US data-centre capacity slated for 2026 was under active construction, with shortages of transformers, switchgear and batteries cited as a main cause, and roughly half of planned 2026 US builds delayed or cancelled. Industry lead-time surveys (Terrapin, Sept 2026 context) put padmount distribution transformers at 40-65 weeks, substation units at 75-110 weeks and large GSUs at 100-150+ weeks; the 3-5 year figure in the thesis applies to large power transformers, not HPS's product. HPS's own evidence of the squeeze is more modest but real: backlog +122% YoY at Dec 31 2025 and +96.9% YoY at June 30 2026, price increases pushed through in fall 2025 and spring 2026, management stating that capacity and lead time now let it command a different commercial situation on data-centre projects, and its own backlog stretching from 6-8 weeks (standard) to two quarters (custom) to four quarters and beyond (multi-year data-centre projects into 2027). The catch: HPS is a build-to-order manufacturer whose own capacity (about C$1.1B today, ~C$1.2B by 2027) is the constraint, so it captures the shortage through volume plus mid-single-digit pricing rather than a commodity price spike.
dossier.analogue: Closest to the bottleneck-play bucket (SanDisk/Micron/Seagate) but a weak version of it. It has the sold-out input (backlog nearly doubled, order book into 2027), the price increases and the multiple re-rate (from a low-teens P/E in 2021-23 to ~28-30x forward). What it lacks is the earnings explosion: adjusted EPS is up ~60% YoY, not 7-21x, because HPS sells engineered hardware at ~31% gross margin with its own factory capacity as the binding limit, not a fungible commodity whose spot price triples. Gross margin (31.5%) is still below 2024's 32.8%, so the pricing side of the bottleneck story is offsetting tariffs and Mexico start-up costs rather than expanding margins. It is not a Dell-style volume-beneficiary-on-a-low-multiple either, since the multiple has already re-rated. Resemblance to the bottleneck analogue: moderate at best; think 'Powell Industries 2023-24' more than 'Micron 2026'.
