dossier.bull_case: Q2 annualises to ~C$1.3B of legacy revenue; add AEG's ~C$326M and 2027 pro forma revenue of C$1.6-1.7B is plausible with capacity at C$1.2B legacy plus AEG. If Mexico absorption lifts gross margin back toward 2024's 32.8% and adjusted EBITDA margin holds 16-17%, pro forma EBITDA approaches C$260-290M and adjusted EPS could reach C$10-12 in 2027 (versus ~C$8.2 consensus for the next FY), which at a sustained 28-30x gives C$300-350, in line with the C$352-372 Street targets and 25-45% upside from C$242. The backlog (nearly double YoY with deliveries into 2027) gives revenue visibility that most industrials lack, price increases have already been absorbed by customers, data-centre demand is over 30% of sales and growing, and half of US data-centre builds being gated by electrical gear means the order funnel is not the constraint. The 34% pullback from the June high on light volume, with the multiple compressed to ~29x forward, is the entry the June buyers did not get.
dossier.bear_case: Gross margin of 31.5% is still below the 32.8% earned in 2024 before the boom, so two years of 'pricing power' have only offset tariffs, copper/steel inflation and Mexico start-up costs; a bottleneck play that cannot expand gross margin is a volume story on a 29x multiple. Backlog fell 6.9% sequentially in Q2 (book-to-bill under 1) even with data-centre demand at its hottest, and if the half of US 2026 data-centre builds that are delayed or cancelled convert into pushed-out or cancelled transformer orders, the +97% YoY backlog comparison turns into negative prints in 2027 against a brutal base. Reported EPS is falling (C$0.79 vs C$1.12), the adjusted-to-GAAP gap is C$2/share, and the company just levered to ~2.7x to buy AEG, a European power-electronics business bought at ~1.1x sales (implying thin margins) that management concedes is dilutive near term. Competitors have committed ~US$2B of transformer capacity since 2023 (Eaton, Siemens Energy, Schneider, ABB), which historically ends transformer up-cycles with lead-time normalisation and price givebacks. Add the controlling shareholder selling C$3.8M of stock at C$276, a dual-class structure, and 34% drawdown momentum, and a de-rating to 18-20x on C$8 of EPS gives C$145-160, roughly 35-40% downside.
dossier.what_confirms: Q3 2026 (late Oct): backlog up sequentially again (book-to-bill back above 1.0x) with gross margin at or above 32% and data-centre revenue share still rising; combined with a first AEG quarter that is neutral-to-accretive on adjusted EPS. That combination would show the shortage is still tightening for HPS specifically and the earnings ramp to C$10+ in 2027 is on track.
dossier.what_kills: A second consecutive sequential backlog decline attributed to data-centre order pushouts or cancellations, gross margin back below 30%, or management walking back the 'pricing stabilised' language with a price cut or lead-time reduction; alternatively, a peer (Eaton, Schneider, ABB) announcing dry-type lead times falling back to normal. Any of these would refute the bottleneck premise and leave a 29x multiple on a decelerating industrial.
dossier.balance_sheet: Pre-deal (Dec 31, 2025): cash C$41.3M, total debt C$96.6M, net debt ~C$55M against FY2025 adjusted EBITDA (up 2% on 2024; absolute figure not retrieved). The Q2 release cites net debt of C$36M at June 30, 2026 driven by working capital, but AEG closed June 29 for C$365M funded from a new US$300M (~C$410M) term loan, so the pro forma net debt is more likely C$400M+ and management's own guide was ~2.7x pro forma TTM net leverage at closing; expect the Q3 balance sheet to show this. Revolver of US$150M available to 2030. Cash generation is modest because working capital scales with the 45% sales growth (inventory and receivables consumed cash in June). No equity raise was used for AEG and none is announced; dilution risk is limited to share-based comp, though the cash-settled units create GAAP earnings volatility with the stock price. Dividend costs ~C$14M a year, easily covered. Rating: adequately financed but no longer net-cash; a data-centre air pocket with 2.7x leverage would be uncomfortable but not existential.
dossier.suggested_sizing: Core 1.5-2% for a risk-aware investor who wants exposure to the electrical-bottleneck theme through a profitable, dividend-paying name; scale to 2.5-3% only if Q3 shows backlog re-accelerating with gross margin above 32%. Treat it as a sleeve 1% if the intent is a pure bottleneck bet, because the earnings torque is far lower than the memory analogues and the multiple has already re-rated.

skeptic.priced_in: Most of the easy money is gone. The stock is up ~118% from its 52-week low, was added to the S&P/TSX Composite at the June 22 peak, has 16 analysts at Buy, and the multiple has roughly doubled versus its 2021-23 range. On the dossier's own numbers the trailing adjusted P/E is ~29-31x (FY2025 adjusted EPS C$6.81 plus the Q2 delta of C$1.04 gives TTM ≥ C$7.85), not the 22x lower bound the dossier quotes; the forward multiple is 24-30x depending on whether the C$8.23 'next-FY' consensus is FY2026 (looks stale given Q2 annualises to ~C$11 adjusted) or FY2027. A 53% adjusted-EPS beat in July produced only a +7% day and then a 15% August slide, which tells you the market is already discounting the adjusted number (much of the GAAP-to-adjusted gap is cash-settled SBC that is a real cost) and the sequential backlog decline. The 34% drawdown removes froth but leaves a growth-industrial multiple that still assumes 2027 EPS well above C$10 and a clean AEG integration. Not undiscovered, not cheap, somewhat de-risked.
skeptic.durability: The thesis as written mis-specifies the bottleneck. The 3-5 year lead times belong to large power/GSU transformers; HPS makes dry-type LV/MV units with 6-8 week standard lead times and up to ~four quarters for custom data-centre work, per management's own comments quoted in the dossier. Dry-type is a lower-barrier segment than LPTs, exposed to Asian imports and to Eaton/Schneider/ABB LV lines, so its pricing power is thinner and shorter-lived; gross margin at 31.5% is still below the 32.8% earned in 2024 despite two rounds of price increases, and management says no further price changes are expected in 2026. The Q4 2025 backlog jump (+74% in one quarter) was a lump of multi-year data-centre orders that is now being burned down (-6.9% QoQ in Q2, book-to-bill under 1). Durability therefore rests on (a) data-centre order intake staying lumpy-but-positive into 2027, (b) tariff policy continuing to shield Mexico/Canada-built product sold into the US (majority of sales, and the growth capacity is in Monterrey, so Section 232 metals tariffs and USMCA compliance are a top-3 risk the dossier underweights), and (c) AEG, a ~1.1x-sales European power-electronics business, not diluting margins for long. Real but a 1-2 year cycle story with the bottleneck already easing at the margins, not a structural moat.
skeptic.evidence_quality: Important caveat: this session's web-search budget was exhausted and every WebFetch to the dossier's sources (stockanalysis, tedmag, powermag, marketbeat, globenewswire) was egress-blocked, so none of the dossier's figures were independently re-verified; the audit is an internal-consistency check plus domain knowledge. On that basis the dossier is above average: the backlog sequence (+122% Dec, +4.1% Q1, -6.9% Q2, +96.9% YoY) reconciles arithmetically, market cap, dividend yield, insider-sale value and AEG deal maths all tie, and the analyst has already flagged its own weakest points (23% share sourced only to a crypto news aggregator, the C$36M net debt figure that cannot coexist with a C$365M cash close funded by a US$300M term loan, memory-based historical multiples). Weaknesses: mixed-date valuation multiples (a May 2026 Seeking Alpha 19x NTM EBITDA quoted alongside a Sept price), an unlabeled consensus EPS year that makes the forward P/E ambiguous, a 'capacity C$1.1B today' figure that is contradicted by a C$1.3B Q2 revenue run-rate, a competitor-capacity catalyst that cites LPT plants irrelevant to dry-type, no explicit interest-cost modelling on ~C$410M of new debt, and Q1 2026 GAAP/adjusted EPS not retrieved so TTM figures are inferred. Q2 primary release figures came via secondary syndications (Yahoo, Manila Times, scanx), which is acceptable but not primary.
corrections: Thesis '23% market share': unverified; the only source is a Phemex crypto-news aggregator. Company and distributors claim only 'largest dry-type transformer manufacturer in North America'. Drop the number or label it unverified.

Thesis 'transformer lead times of 3 to 5 years': applies to large power/GSU transformers, not HPS's product. Per management quotes in the dossier, HPS dry-type lead times are 6-8 weeks (standard), ~two quarters (custom) and up to ~four quarters for multi-year data-centre projects. Padmount/substation industry lead times are 40-110 weeks.

Thesis 'half of US data-center builds are delayed by electrical gear': the underlying Bloomberg-sourced reporting says roughly half of planned 2026 US builds are delayed or cancelled, with transformer/switchgear/battery shortages cited as one main cause alongside power interconnection, permitting and financing. Causation is overstated.

Dossier valuation '~22-30x on adjusted trailing EPS': the 22x lower bound is inconsistent with the dossier's own data. FY2025 adjusted EPS C$6.81 plus the Q2 2026 YoY delta of C$1.04 gives TTM adjusted EPS of at least ~C$7.85 (before any Q1 delta), i.e. ~29-31x at C$242.

Dossier 'forward P/E ~28-30x on ~C$8.2-8.8 consensus': the C$8.23 'next-FY' figure is roughly flat with TTM adjusted EPS and below the Q2 annualised run-rate (~C$11), so it is either FY2026 consensus that is stale or a GAAP-basis number. Label the year; if H1 2026 adjusted EPS is ~C$4.5-5, FY2026 adjusted of C$9.5-10 implies ~24-26x, not 28-30x.

Dossier 'capacity about C$1.1B today, ~C$1.2B by 2027': Q2 2026 revenue of C$324.8M annualises to ~C$1.3B, above the stated current capacity. Either the capacity figure is stale/defined at normal utilisation or includes only certain plants. Also, the bull case's C$1.6-1.7B 2027 pro forma revenue exceeds the dossier's own 2027 capacity (C$1.2B) plus AEG (C$326M) = ~C$1.53B.

Dossier/bear case '2.7x pro forma net leverage': that was management's Feb 2026 guide on FY2025 EBITDA. On TTM adjusted EBITDA at June 30 2026 (~C$165M+ standalone, more with AEG) and ~C$400M pro forma net debt, leverage is closer to 2.2-2.5x. Estimate, not verified.

Dossier 'trailing EV/EBITDA ~27x': on the dossier's own EV (C$3.2-3.3B) and TTM adjusted EBITDA (~C$165-180M) trailing EV/adj EBITDA is ~18-20x; 27x would require GAAP EBITDA burdened by cash-settled SBC. Also the '19x NTM EBITDA' is from a May 2026 article at a different share price.

Dossier competitor-capacity catalyst (Siemens Energy Charlotte LPT plant, Eaton South Carolina, '~US$2B industry-wide'): these are predominantly large-power / liquid-filled transformer capacity, not dry-type, so they do not directly normalise HPS's segment. The relevant competitive threat is dry-type imports (Asia) and Eaton/Schneider/ABB/Hubbell LV lines, which is a tariff-policy question the dossier underweights.

Dossier net debt C$36M at June 30, 2026: cannot be reconciled with the June 29 AEG cash close funded by a US$300M term loan; likely a pre-financing or misread figure. Do not use it for EV; use ~C$400M pro forma until the Q3 balance sheet is published.

Q2 2026 GAAP earnings fell partly because cash-settled share units are marked to a rising stock price; with the stock down 34% since June, Q3 GAAP EPS will get an optical tailwind from an SBC reversal. Adjusted EPS strips this out in both directions, so the adjusted-vs-GAAP gap is a quality-of-earnings issue the dossier should call out explicitly rather than treat as noise.
skeptic.one_line: HPS.A C$242: genuine 45% sales / 60% adj-EPS growth with data centres >30% of sales, but the thesis mis-cites LPT lead times and an unverified 23% share; ~29-31x trailing adj, 34% off June high, backlog -7% QoQ, AEG dilutive near term, Mexico/tariff exposure. Interesting, not compelling: wait for Q3 (late Oct) book-to-bill >1 and GM >32% before sizing above 1%.

dossier.name: Powell Industries, Inc.
dossier.market_cap: ~$6.6B at $181.07 on 2026-09-05 (~36.5M shares post 3-for-1 split effective 2026-04-06); EV ~$6.0B net of $634M cash
dossier.business: Powell designs and builds custom, engineered-to-order medium/low-voltage switchgear, power control rooms (prefabricated electrical houses), bus duct and related protection/automation systems, plus field service. Customers are oil & gas/LNG/petrochemical operators, electric utilities, light-rail transit, and increasingly hyperscale data centers (grouped under "commercial and other industrial"). Manufacturing is concentrated in Houston (Jacintoport fabrication yard) with additional North American plants; projects are fixed-price and recognised over time, so revenue lags orders by 12-30 months.
dossier.why_now: The bottleneck is North American medium-voltage electrical gear: third-party trackers put 15kV MV switchgear lead times at 52-80 weeks and 38kV at 78-104 weeks versus ~24 weeks pre-pandemic, and power transformers at ~128 weeks with prices up ~77% since 2019 (Terrapin CG / Industrial Sage, 2026). Data-center capex is colliding with that constrained supply. Powell's own numbers show demand hitting the wall in fiscal Q3 2026 (quarter ended 2026-06-30): record orders of $934M (+158% y/y), book-to-bill of 3.0x, backlog $2.4B (+35% q/q, +73% vs 2025-09-30), anchored by a $400M+ data-center award that is the largest in its 79-year history and burns through fiscal 2028. The catch that makes this different from the memory-chip template is that the constraint is Powell's own factory floor, not a sold-out commodity input: revenue grew only 9% and gross margin was flat at 30.6% in the same quarter, and management describes pricing as "stable", not spiking. The thesis therefore hinges on capacity additions (Jacintoport +335k sq ft completing by end of FY26, a ~300k sq ft leased plant being readied, a $70-100M owned factory under evaluation) converting the backlog into a revenue step-up in FY27-FY28.
dossier.analogue: Closest to the bottleneck-play template (SanDisk/Micron/Seagate) in the order book: sold-out capacity, 3.0x book-to-bill, backlog equal to ~2 years of revenue. But it resembles it only loosely — the key ingredients of that trade (input price spike, earnings up 7-21x) are absent: Q3 EPS grew 8% y/y and gross margin was flat at 30.6% because Powell sells fixed-price engineered projects and adds capacity rather than raising price. It is also not a Dell-style volume beneficiary on a low multiple, since it trades at ~35x trailing and ~26-28x forward. Best description: a capacity-gated backlog compounder whose multiple already re-rated (~$7 in 2020 to a $321.94 close on 2026-05-11) and has since given back 44%.

dossier.bull_case: Backlog of $2.4B is ~2x TTM revenue and ~29% of it (as of March) sits in commercial/data center where Q3 revenue grew 54%; the $400M+ hyperscaler order alone adds ~$40-50M per quarter through FY28. dossier.bear_case: This is a fixed-price project business, not a commodity with a price spike: gross margin is flat at 30.6%, pricing is "stable", and revenue grew 9% while backlog grew 73% — capacity, not demand, sets the P&L. Management's own framing (via Cantor, 2026-08-14) is that the $70-100M owned plant supports growth beyond the current backlog, so a large revenue step-up is 18-24 months away and depends on execution across five facilities for a single mega order. Consensus FY26 EPS of ~$5.35 is only ~7% above FY25's $4.99; the stock still trades at ~35x that. Petrochemical revenue fell 49% and Powell was a single-digit-P/E, oil-and-gas cyclical as recently as 2020; if data center orders normalise after a lumpy $934M quarter and the FY27 multiple compresses to 20x on ~$6.9 EPS, the stock is ~$138 (-24%). dossier.market_cap: Approximately $3.2-3.5B (early Sept 2026; sources quote $3.18B-$3.47B at share prices of roughly $168-$190; ~19.8M basic shares at end-2025, ~22.4M diluted in Q1 2026). EV approx. $2.5B given ~$0.7B net cash (stockanalysis.com, date not stated, ~Aug/Sept 2026).
dossier.business: Centrus sells enriched uranium (SWU and natural uranium components) to nuclear utilities in the US and abroad through its LEU segment, today mostly as a trader/broker of material it buys from suppliers (chiefly Russia's TENEX and Orano) rather than from its own production. Its Technical Solutions segment does government contract work, principally operating the DOE-funded 16-centrifuge HALEU demonstration cascade in Piketon, Ohio. The company is now building out commercial LEU and HALEU enrichment capacity at Piketon (Fluor as EPC, Oak Ridge centrifuge manufacturing), with first commercial output targeted for 2029.
dossier.why_now: The bottleneck is real but it is a 2028-2032 bottleneck, not a 2026 one. Western enrichment supply is capped (Urenco, Orano, Centrus' future plant), Russia supplied roughly a quarter of US enrichment before the Prohibiting Russian Uranium Imports Act (effective Aug 11, 2024; DOE waivers only permitted until Jan 1, 2028; ban runs to 2040), and Russia retaliated with export licensing restrictions in Nov 2024. Spot SWU sits at $200-215/SWU and long-term at $181-183 (month-end Aug 2026, UxC/TradeTech via industry trackers) versus roughly $50-60 pre-2022. Washington is paying to fix it: DOE awarded $2.7B on Jan 7, 2026 in three $900M task orders (Centrus, Orano, General Matter), and Centrus signed its $900M task order (up to ~$1.07B with $170M of optional HALEU purchases) in Q2 2026. The catch for the framework: Centrus' current P&L is a legacy trading book with 20-year contracts and Russian-sourced material, so the price spike shows up as only a +3% average SWU price in Q2 2026 while volumes fell 23%; the 2028 waiver cliff first threatens Centrus' own supply before its own capacity arrives in 2029. This is a government-backed capacity build (Intel analogue) with a bottleneck backdrop, not a SanDisk/Micron-style earnings explosion.
dossier.analogue: Closest to the government-backed turnaround (Intel) analogue, with only partial resemblance to the bottleneck (SanDisk/Micron/Seagate) analogue. Similarities to Intel: sole domestic supplier of a strategic input, ~$0.9-1.07B of federal milestone money, multi-year capex program ($350-500M in 2026 alone) before any new revenue, stock washed out (~63% below its Oct 2025 high), heavy short interest (~27% of float, Aug 2026). Where it fails the bottleneck test: the input is sold out and prices have spiked, but Centrus' earnings are not going up 7-21x; Q1 2026 net income fell 63% y/y and Q2 gross profit fell y/y despite revenue growth because Centrus mostly resells purchased SWU on legacy contract prices. The multiple (roughly 50-60x forward P/E) is already a re-rated multiple, so the 'price spike plus multiple expansion' engine of the 2026 memory winners is not available here. Resemblance to Intel: moderate-to-close; to the bottleneck plays: weak until 2029.

dossier.bull_case: Centrus is the only US-owned, licensed, operating enricher, and the only public way to own Western SWU capacity. It has $1.9B of cash, $0.9-1.07B of DOE milestone funding, a $4.5B backlog to 2040, prepayment-bearing HALEU contracts with X-energy (definitive) and Oklo (LOI), an EPC partner (Fluor), and centrifuge manufacturing already running at Oak Ridge. If Piketon delivers first capacity in 2029 into a market where spot SWU is $200-215 and long-term $181-183 (Aug 2026), and the Russian ban plus 2028 waiver expiry removes ~20-25% of US supply, Centrus would move from reselling SWU at ~28% gross margin to producing it at manufacturer margins. On the bull math, a plant sized for 12 MTU/yr HALEU plus several million SWU of LEU could generate multiples of today's ~$120M annual gross profit; the stock at ~$170 (Sept 2026) already trades at an EV of ~$2.5B, ~0.55x backlog, ~63% below its Oct 2025 high, with ~27% of float short and analyst targets clustered at $200-300 (Northland $300). Any evidence that execution is on schedule, plus a short squeeze, could take the stock back toward the $250 area of year-end 2025 (+45%) without needing the 2025 peak multiple.
dossier.bear_case: The current business is shrinking in profitability while the new one is years away and capital-hungry. Q1 2026 net income fell 63% y/y and Q2 gross margin dropped to ~28% from ~35%; SWU volume fell 23% in Q2 while average price rose only 3%, so the SWU price spike is not reaching Centrus' P&L. Its largest supplier is Russia's TENEX: after Jan 1, 2028 no waivers are available, so the 2028 'shortage' first removes Centrus' own product before its 2029 plant arrives, and Russia has already shown it will restrict export licenses (Nov 2024 decree). Capex is $350-500M in 2026 alone with a multi-billion-dollar total build; the balance sheet already carries $1.18B of converts (0% 2032 and 2.25% 2030) and a $1B ATM that raised $524M in 2025 at 15% share dilution; more equity is plausible if milestones slip. At ~50-60x forward earnings versus a 17x own-history average, the stock is not cheap on anything except backlog, and ~$2.4B of that backlog was contingent on the plant being built. Competitors Orano and General Matter received equal $900M DOE awards and Urenco is expanding in New Mexico, so Centrus is not the sole beneficiary of US policy. If H2 2026 revenue comes in at the low end (~$197M) and margins keep compressing, a de-rating to 30x on ~$3 of EPS points to ~$90-100, below the July 2026 low of $142.
dossier.what_confirms: A disclosed, dated schedule showing the first Oak Ridge centrifuges installed and the first commercial LEU/HALEU cascade in cold/hot commissioning at Piketon on or ahead of the 2029 target, funded from existing cash plus DOE milestone payments and customer prepayments with no further ATM issuance; plus a Q3/Q4 2026 print where SWU average selling price rises meaningfully (well above the +3% seen in Q2) as legacy contracts roll into $180+ long-term pricing.
dossier.what_kills: Any of: (1) DOE denies or delays the third TENEX import waiver for 2026-27 deliveries, or Russia refuses export licenses, forcing supply shortfalls or expensive spot cover; (2) a slip of first-capacity timing beyond 2029 or a cost overrun forcing a new equity raise at these prices; (3) a rival (Orano, General Matter, Urenco) reaching commercial US HALEU/LEU output first and pulling the contingent $2.4B LEU backlog away.
dossier.balance_sheet: Cash, equivalents and restricted cash $1,901.9M at Jun 30, 2026 (down from $1,960.1M at Dec 31, 2025, i.e. ~$58M consumed in H1 while capex ramps). Long-term debt $1,177.5M: $805M 0% convertible notes due 2032 (upsized, Q3 2025) and $402.5M 2.25% convertible notes due 2030 (Nov 2024). Net cash ~$0.7B. Equity: $1B ATM program launched Nov 2025, $523.7M raised in 2025; shares outstanding ~19.8M at end-2025 (up ~15% in a year), diluted ~22.4M in Q1 2026. Dilution risk is material: 2026 capex guidance of $350-500M plus the multi-year build exceed the ~$120M annual operating cash generation, so the company will burn cash; the $900M DOE award is paid only against milestones, and the converts add ~5.5-6M shares of potential dilution if in the money (conversion prices not found). No pension-style legacy liabilities were checked. Overall: funded for roughly the next 2-3 years of construction, but not through to first cash from new capacity without either milestone receipts, prepayments, or further issuance.
dossier.suggested_sizing: Sleeve 1% (build in two halves, one now and one after the Q3 2026 print in early Nov); not core. A washed-out stock with 27% short interest and a $200-215 spot SWU backdrop is tradeable, but ~50-60x forward earnings on declining H1 profits, a 2028 Russian supply cliff and 2029 first-capacity make it a policy-and-execution binary, not a bottleneck earnings play.

dossier.business: Modine makes thermal-management hardware. Its Climate Solutions segment sells Airedale-branded data-center cooling (air-cooled chillers such as the Turbo Chill 3+MW, CDUs/liquid-cooling, containment, fan walls) to hyperscalers and colocation operators, plus commercial HVAC&R and heat-transfer coils. Customers are paying up-front to reserve Modine's cooling capacity: on May 26, 2026 an undisclosed hyperscaler (Hunterbrook alleges Google) signed a >$4B long-term capacity agreement for CY2027-2029 with a $165M cash prepayment, and management logged a third consecutive record order quarter that doubled backlog. But unlike Micron/SanDisk, Modine is the constrained party, not the price-setter: Q1 FY27 (June 2026) data-center gross margin fell 960bp YoY to 20.2% because component shortages capped production and stranded overhead (450-550bp hit), and free cash flow was -$5.0M. skeptic.priced_in: Most of it. The dossier's own numbers say so: backlog doubled, adjusted EPS +73%, the multiple has gone from mid-teens to ~27-30x forward, and the stock is still up 42% YTD after a 24% drawdown from the June 30 high. The dossier understates one thing on the priced-in side: Q2 adjusted EPS of $8.17 annualises to ~$32.7, which is already above the $31.08 FY2027 consensus it quotes, so the "+25% 2027 EPS growth" framing is really growth off a stale FY2026 estimate ($26.71 implies H2 2026 EPS of only ~$6.5/quarter, below what was just printed with guidance raised). Either consensus has moved up to ~$29-31 for 2026 (which is what makes stockanalysis's 27.1x forward tie out) and the stock is cheaper on 2026 than the dossier says, or the Street expects H2 to fall back, which is itself a warning about the $392M tariff-recovery flattering of Q2. Either way a new buyer at ~$814 is paying ~26-27x for 2027 earnings that the Street already assumes are flat-to-up from the current run-rate; the upside case in the dossier (+14% to +20%) is modest for the risk, and the bear cases (-27% to -34%) are entirely multiple-driven and require no operational miss. "Late" is the right call.
skeptic.durability: The bottleneck is real but supply-side and therefore self-limiting: Caterpillar is targeting ~3x 2024 large-recip capacity by 2030 and restarting a mothballed 10 MW platform in Q4 2026, while Cummins, Wartsila, Rolls-Royce mtu, INNIO and the turbine OEMs (GE Vernova, Siemens Energy, Mitsubishi) are all adding capacity into the same 2028 window. Reciprocating gensets are the stopgap for developers who could not get gas turbines; when turbine slots reopen the marginal order for a 10 MW recip disappears. The 41% of backlog beyond 12 months is only ~$29.5B and is concentrated in the segment most exposed to hyperscaler capex timing and to novel counterparties (the 2 GW AIP/Monarch order is a first-of-its-kind developer, not a hyperscaler; cancellation and financing risk there is not discussed). Price realisation of ~$600M/quarter is the most fragile piece: it comes from scarcity, and scarcity is exactly what the capex plan is designed to remove. The construction/mining 60% is a genuine second leg but is cyclical and has not been shown to be turning. I would call the bottleneck durable through 2027 and open to question from 2028, which is precisely when the 2027-2029 capex lands. That is a two-year window, not a structural moat.
skeptic.evidence_quality: The analyst has been unusually honest about what is derived versus reported (book-to-bill, forward P/E arithmetic, the stale $63B backlog, the dealer-blog origin of the 'sold out through 2027' wording), and the headline figures (sales $20.5B +24%, adj EPS $8.17, backlog $72.1B +92%, ME&T FCF $5.1B, guidance raised to mid-to-high teens, capex $3.5B, 3x large-recip target) are mutually consistent and consistent with the 2025 base year (FY2025 sales $67.6B, adj EPS $19.06, Q2 2025 EPS $4.72). Weaknesses: (1) no primary-source verification of the P&E segment figures, and the +17% growth on $8.2B does not reconcile with the ~$7.8B Energy & Transportation segment Caterpillar reported for Q2 2025 unless the segment was redefined, which the dossier does not mention; (2) the FY2026 consensus EPS looks stale; (3) ME&T-only leverage, gross margin, Cat Financial credit metrics, short interest and the reported new credit lines were not found; (4) the peer P/E comparison mixes a stale TTM median (15.5x) with current forward multiples (Deere 30x); (5) nothing on customer concentration or counterparty quality within the P&E backlog. I could not run any of my own checks this session (search budget exhausted, all fetches blocked), so nothing in the dossier has been independently confirmed by this review; the corrections below are from arithmetic and internal consistency only.
corrections: why_now: the Q2 2025 backlog was ~$37.5B, not $35B ($35B was the Q1 2025 figure). The dossier's own Q2 2026 delta (+$34.6B to $72.1B) implies a $37.5B base.

Power & Energy: $8.2B at +17% YoY implies a ~$7.0B Q2 2025 base, but Caterpillar reported ~$7.8B for the Energy & Transportation segment in Q2 2025. Either the segment was redefined in 2026 (transportation/rail/marine carved out) or the growth rate/base is wrong; the dossier should state which and cite the restated comparative. Related: with Construction Industries at ~$6.2B in Q2 2025, P&E at $8.2B is probably larger than CI, not 'nearly as large'.

Valuation: FY2026 consensus EPS of $26.71 is almost certainly stale. H1 2026 adjusted EPS is $13.71, so $26.71 implies H2 of ~$6.5/quarter versus $8.17 just reported with guidance raised. Post-Q2 consensus is more plausibly ~$29-31, which is what reconciles stockanalysis's 27.1x forward. The '~30.5x 2026' figure and the bear-case '$27 of 2026 EPS' should be re-based; conversely, the '+25% 2027 EPS growth' in how_far_run_note is growth off a stale base, and Q2 annualised ($32.7) already exceeds the $31.08 FY2027 consensus.

dossier.name: Lumentum Holdings Inc.
dossier.market_cap: ~$79B (stockanalysis.com, 4 Sep 2026); ~$69B per multiples.vc snapshot in Aug 2026. Non-GAAP diluted share count 101.1M (Q4 FY26), plus 2.88M Nvidia preferred converting 1:1.
dossier.business: Lumentum designs and manufactures indium-phosphide (InP) laser chips (EMLs, CW/pump lasers, ultra-high-power lasers for co-packaged optics), 800G/1.6T optical transceivers, and optical circuit switches (OCS) used in AI data-center networks, plus a legacy telecom/industrial laser franchise. Customers are hyperscalers, transceiver makers and Nvidia; in fiscal Q4 2026 (quarter ended 27 Jun 2026) components were $649.4M and systems $356.9M of $1.01B revenue. Nvidia became a strategic shareholder in March 2026 via a $2B convertible preferred with laser capacity access rights.
dossier.why_now: This is a sold-out-input story. Management says EML and pump-laser demand exceeds supply by roughly 30% even after adding 20% capacity (May 2026 call), that all EML capacity is locked under long-term agreements through calendar 2027, and the CEO said in March 2026 "we're sold out really until the end of 2027, we see no end in sight" — even after a planned ~50% InP output increase from Q4 CY25 to Q4 CY26. Lumentum is described by several industry sources as the only supplier shipping 200G-per-lane EMLs (needed for 1.6T modules) at volume, with 200G already >25% of EML revenue and guided to >50% by mid-2027; analysts expect double-digit price increases on 200G EMLs in 2026 given no viable second source. Layered on top: an OCS backlog >$400M with most shipments in 2H26-2027 and a multi-year "multibillion-dollar" OCS deal with a hyperscaler (announced at OFC, March 2026), and Nvidia's $2B investment tied to a multibillion purchase commitment and future capacity access rights. The operative question is not whether the bottleneck exists — the numbers confirm it — but that the stock is already up roughly 7x in 12 months and trades ~50x forward earnings, so the bottleneck is largely priced.
dossier.analogue: Closest to the bottleneck plays (Micron/SanDisk/Seagate): sold-out input, price increases, earnings up several-fold (non-GAAP EPS $0.88 in Q4 FY25 to $3.23 in Q4 FY26, +267%; quarterly revenue +109% YoY), multiple re-rated (stock +~680% in 12 months). Two important differences: (1) Lumentum's volumes are capacity-capped (undershipping demand by ~30%) and much of its output is under multi-year LTAs, so it does not get the memory-style spot-price spike — its upside comes from mix (200G ASPs) and capacity adds that land in 2027-2028; (2) the memory names re-rated from single-digit to mid-teens P/Es, whereas LITE already sits at ~50x forward and ~16x annualized run-rate sales. So: same category, but the market is ~12-18 months further along in pricing it than it was for the memory names in early 2026.

dossier.bull_case: Demand exceeds supply by ~30% and every unit of new InP capacity (+50% by Q4 CY26, +Greensboro in 2028) is pre-sold under LTAs, so revenue growth is a capacity schedule rather than a demand forecast: $1.25B in the Sep-26 quarter (guide) toward $2B/quarter at 40% operating margin by 2028. Mix shifts to 200G EMLs (>50% of EML revenue by mid-2027) with double-digit price increases carry non-GAAP gross margin from 50.4% toward the mid-50s, and OCS adds a >$1B calendar-2027 revenue line that did not exist two years ago. On $8B annualized revenue at 40% OM, non-GAAP EPS could approach ~$26 (my estimate); at a 40-45x multiple — justified while the company is the sole volume 200G EML source and Nvidia is a shareholder with capacity rights — that supports $1,050-1,170, in line with the $1,100-1,148 Street targets and ~25-35% upside from $870. Balance sheet is net cash (~$2.7B cash vs $1.64B debt), FCF turned positive ($300M in FY26), and short interest of ~10-20% of float provides squeeze fuel on further beats.
dossier.bear_case: The stock already discounts the sold-out story: ~50x forward earnings, ~16x run-rate sales, ~7x in 12 months, and it fell 14% after an 8% beat on revenue and 16% beat on EPS in August. Growth is capacity-limited, so upside surprises are structurally capped near the capacity ramp (~24% QoQ) while any yield or fab-conversion slip shows up immediately as a miss — and the two big capacity levers (Greensboro, OCS scale) do not deliver until 2027-2028. LTAs fix volumes and, likely, pricing, so the memory-style price spike that drove 7-21x earnings gains elsewhere is not available here. Second-sourcing risk is real: Broadcom, Mitsubishi Electric and Coherent have all shown 200G EML capability and TrendForce projects monthly EML/CW-DFB capacity of 50.7M units industry-wide in 2026; Chinese suppliers are also being pulled in. Customer concentration around Nvidia and one hyperscaler OCS deal means a pause in AI capex (the scenario the memory names also face) would compress the multiple back toward 20-25x on lower estimates — a 50-60% drawdown from here. The remaining $1.54B of converts are classified short-term and have historically been settled in stock (10.7M shares in FY26), so dilution continues.
dossier.what_confirms: Fiscal Q1 2027 (report ~10 Nov 2026) revenue at or above $1.275B with non-GAAP OM ≥40% and Q2 guidance implying a further ≥15% QoQ step, plus explicit commentary that 200G EML ASPs are rising and that LTA coverage now extends into 2028 — i.e. the capacity ramp is converting to revenue without yield or margin leakage. A second data point: OCS revenue actually hitting the $100M/quarter run-rate by the Dec-2026 quarter.
dossier.what_kills: Any statement that the EML supply-demand gap has closed (customers no longer undershipped, LTAs being renegotiated or capacity "available") or evidence that Broadcom/Coherent/Mitsubishi are shipping 200G EMLs in volume — that would remove the sole-source premium. Operationally: a fiscal Q1/Q2 2027 revenue miss versus the $1.225-1.275B guide or gross margin falling back below ~48%, indicating the ramp is yield-constrained. Externally: a hyperscaler capex cut or Nvidia signalling optics design changes (e.g., CPO reducing pluggable EML demand faster than UHP laser revenue replaces it).

Net cash ~ $1.1B. FY26 operating cash flow $751.4M, investing outflow $785.5M, FCF roughly +$300M (first positive year after two years of burn). Dilution: $1,124.9M of converts were equitized in FY26 for ~10.7M shares (producing the $7.8B non-cash GAAP loss on extinguishment); the remaining $1.54B of converts are deep in the money and likely to convert; the 2.88M Nvidia preferred shares convert 1:1 (≈2.8% of the 101.1M diluted count). input.name: Bloom Energy
input.thesis: Fuel cells as on-site power when grid interconnection takes years; running at capacity through 2026; $2.5B Brookfield deal; 30 percent ITC from 2026. Test how much is priced in.

dossier.name: Bloom Energy Corporation
dossier.market_cap: ~$70B implied at the Sep 4, 2026 close of $252.87 (Motley Fool cited ~$60B at ~$207-217 on Aug 27, 2026; stockanalysis.com showed $74.48B at $266.18 in early Sep 2026). Exact share count not found in snippets.
dossier.business: Bloom sells solid-oxide fuel cell (SOFC) "Energy Servers" that generate on-site electricity from natural gas (also biogas/hydrogen) without a grid interconnection, plus multi-year service contracts and, historically, electricity under PPAs. Since 2025 the buyer base has shifted from commercial/industrial customers to AI data-center power: hyperscalers (Oracle up to 2.8 GW MSA), utilities (AEP up to 1 GW, $2.65B), neo-clouds and colos, financed largely via Brookfield's project framework. Product revenue was 88% of Q2 2026 sales.
dossier.why_now: The bottleneck is grid interconnection: utility grid upgrades take 2+ years while Bloom delivered one AI-factory order in 55 days against a 90-day commitment (Utility Dive/Seeking Alpha, 2025-26). That has produced a genuine earnings inflection: Q2 2026 revenue $1,065M (+165.5% y/y, +42% q/q), non-GAAP operating income $239.6M (~8.4x y/y), non-GAAP EPS $0.78 (~7.8x), guidance raised twice this year to $3.9-4.2B revenue (~100% growth) and $2.55-2.85 non-GAAP EPS (~3.6x). Three specific drivers: (1) fuel cells regained a 30% Section 48E ITC for projects beginning construction after Dec 31, 2025 (no adders), which JPMorgan estimated cuts effective cost from ~8c/kWh to ~5-6c/kWh; (2) Brookfield expanded its financing framework from $5B (Oct 13, 2025) to $25B (Jun 30, 2026); (3) Fremont capacity doubling from 1 GW to 2 GW by end-2026 (~$100M capex). The important caveat for the framework: management said on the Q2 call it is "not capacity or order constrained," and the AEP contract priced at ~$2,950/kW came in BELOW Mizuho's $3,100/kW ASP estimate, so this is a volume story, not a sold-out/price-spike story.
dossier.analogue: Closest to the SanDisk/Micron/Seagate bottleneck-play analogue in earnings shape (revenue +166%, non-GAAP op income ~8x, EPS ~8x, and a re-rated multiple), but the fit is only partial: the scarce input is grid power, not Bloom's own product; management explicitly says it is not capacity- or order-constrained; there is no evidence of a price spike (AEP ASP ~$2,950/kW below Mizuho's $3,100 estimate); and the multiple has already re-rated to ~94x guided 2026 non-GAAP EPS versus GE Vernova at ~38x forward. It has none of the Dell "low multiple" character and, with the Hunterbrook/Crossroads scandium and backlog disputes, carries a binary element more like a short-report battleground than a Moderna-style readout. Net: a bottleneck-derivative play whose bottleneck-phase earnings surge is largely already delivered and priced.

dossier.bull_case: Grid queues stay at 2+ years, so every hyperscaler and neo-cloud needs bridge/primary on-site power now; Bloom is the only SOFC vendor at GW scale with all major U.S. hyperscalers validated. The 2 GW plant runs full in 2027 at ~$3,000/kW product ASP, i.e. ~$6B product revenue plus service, at the guided ~34% gross margin and mid-20s non-GAAP operating margin — roughly $1.5B operating income and ~$4+ non-GAAP EPS, double 2026. The 30% ITC lowers customer effective cost by ~25-35% (JPM: 8c to 5-6c/kWh), pulling forward price-sensitive demand; Brookfield's $25B framework removes customer balance-sheet friction; Oracle's remaining 1.6 GW and a Motley Fool-style path to a $50B backlog would keep growth >50% into 2028. Company claims supply-chain visibility for 25 GW/yr, neutralising the scandium scare. At 60x 2027 EPS for 100%+ growth the PEG is under 1; S&P 500 inclusion (Sep 21) broadens ownership. Analyst upside to $295 median implies ~17%; a re-rate on 2027 guidance could push toward the UBS $300 target.
dossier.bear_case: At ~94x 2026 guided EPS and ~17x sales, the stock already discounts several years of flawless execution while the near-term data are decelerating: guidance implies H2 revenue only ~15-30% above H1, and management admits it is not capacity- or order-constrained — the opposite of a sold-out bottleneck. Backlog quality is contested: audited RPO was $492.6M at Mar 31, 2026 versus a marketed $20B; 74% of Q4 2025 revenue came through part-owned Brookfield JVs with unnamed end customers; AEP's 1 GW slipped from 2028 to 'no later than 2030' after its developer Crusoe exited, and its hyperscaler backstop can walk for cost +10%. Pricing is soft, not rising (AEP at ~$2,950/kW below the $3,100 sell-side ASP). Scandium: Hunterbrook/Crossroads argue 5 GW needs ~220 t of scandium oxide against ~240 t global supply, with Chinese routes traced through Thailand, Japan, Korea; a class action is live. Grid relief (GE Vernova/Siemens turbine capacity, transmission fixes) or an AI-capex pause would hit a $70B name with $2.5B of converts due 2030. Downside to sell-side low targets ($176 Wells, $188 Jefferies) is 25-30%; a reversion to 40x a $3.00 2027 EPS is ~$120, or -50%.

dossier.market_cap: ~US$39-44B (calc: 124.66M post-offering shares x ~$312 pre-jump close of ~Sep 2 / ~$349 implied after the +11.7% move on Sep 3, 2026). Third-party snapshots: $41.33B (Google Finance, early Aug 2026), $48.9B (stockanalysis, date unclear). Sep 4 close not found.
dossier.business: Celestica is a Toronto-based EMS/ODM that designs and builds data-center hardware: high-speed Ethernet switches (400G/800G, 1.6T ramping), storage and AI/ML compute racks, sold mainly to hyperscalers and "digital native" AI labs through its Connectivity & Cloud Solutions (CCS) segment, which was 81% of Q2 2026 revenue ($3.81B, +84% y/y). Its Hardware Platform Solutions (HPS) line, ~$1.9B in Q2, is Celestica-designed (ODM) product, carrying higher margins than build-to-print. A smaller ATS segment ($888M, +8%) serves aerospace/defense, industrial, healthtech and capital equipment.
dossier.why_now: The framework "bottleneck" here is not Celestica's own product but AI-cluster networking capacity: the shift to 800G and the 1.6T generation (Broadcom Tomahawk 6) is being deployed faster than the supply chain can build it. Management says demand "exceeds the revenue figures the company has provided," that custom silicon, memory, 40+ layer PCBs, power and optical components are on allocation with lead times over 52 weeks, and that customers are therefore giving binding 12-18 month forecasts and, in some cases, capacity discussions into 2028-2029. Celestica has 10 active 1.6T programs building in H2 2026 and two named multi-billion-dollar rack programs (OpenAI/Broadcom custom accelerator racks with initial deliveries late 2026 and mass production 2027; AMD Helios scale-up racks in 2027). On July 27, 2026 it raised 2026 revenue guidance to $20.5B (+65%) and adjusted EPS to $11.30 (+87%) and said 2027 growth would exceed 65%. The "why now" for the stock is that it is roughly 26% below its June 2, 2026 high after a $3B equity raise at $310 (Aug 5-6) knocked it down ~14%, and the Sep 3 Broadcom/Dell/HPE readthrough just snapped a three-month slide.
dossier.analogue: Closest to the Dell-pattern volume beneficiary, but at a growth multiple rather than Dell's low one. Like Dell, Celestica captures unit volume of AI racks/switches with thin (8%) operating margins and is itself constrained by (and a price-taker on) the real bottleneck inputs; it is not the sold-out input whose price spikes, so earnings are compounding at ~1.9x/yr, not the 7-21x of SanDisk/Micron/Seagate. Where it differs from Dell: its ODM (HPS) mix and 800G switch share give it more pricing/margin leverage, and the market already pays ~30x 2026 EPS (Dell-type names trade in the teens). Not a binary readout and not a government turnaround. Fit: Dell analogue, ~70% match; bottleneck-play elements ~30%.

dossier.bull_case: Celestica is the share-gaining ODM for AI networking at the exact moment 800G goes mainstream and 1.6T starts: CCS grew 84% in Q2 2026, HPS (own-design, higher margin) 58%, adjusted operating margin made a record 8.2% and guidance has been raised three times in seven months (from $17.0B/$8.75 to $20.5B/$11.30). Management says 2027 revenue growth will exceed 65%, i.e. >$33.8B, with EPS growing faster, implying >$18.65 adj EPS pre-dilution (~$17.5 post). Component allocation and 52-week-plus lead times have forced customers into binding 12-18 month forecasts, and capacity talks reach 2028-2029, so the revenue visibility is unusually good for an EMS. Two named multi-billion-dollar rack programs (OpenAI/Broadcom, AMD Helios) are incremental to the switch franchise. The $3B raise removes balance-sheet constraint (pro forma net cash ~$2.8B) for the working-capital surge. If 2027 EPS of ~$17.5 is delivered and the stock holds 25x, that is ~$440 (+25% from ~$349), consistent with consensus $440 and JPMorgan's $485; hold 30x and it is ~$525 (+50%). The Sep 3 Broadcom/Dell/HPE readthrough shows the demand signal is intact after the summer wobble.
dossier.bear_case: This is an 8%-margin assembler priced at ~31x current-year EPS with three customers at ~65% of revenue. Any one hyperscaler pausing a build, shifting to a second source, or insourcing rack integration can push revenue timing out a quarter, and at this multiple a miss vs the >65%-growth 2027 bar is a 30-40% de-rating to peer levels (~18-20x trailing). Input costs (memory, custom silicon, PCBs) are rising materially and Celestica is a price-taker; gross margin is only ~11.5%, so a 50 bp squeeze is ~4% of EBIT. The company just issued $3B of stock at $310 (8.4% dilution, ~5x its 2026 FCF) to fund working capital and $1B of capex, which tells you cash conversion is weak in a boom (H1 FCF $285M on $8.75B revenue, ~3%); if 2027 growth is >65%, inventory and receivables scale with it and another raise or revolver draw is plausible. The stock already fell 34% from its June high before the Sep 3 bounce, the Aug 6 downgrade to Hold and the "Celestica Faces Dilution" theme show sentiment is fragile, and the June 45x forward multiple is the ceiling the market already rejected. Downside scenario: 2027 EPS of ~$14 (growth 30%, not 65%) at 20x = $280, -20%.
dossier.what_confirms: A Q3 2026 print (~Oct 26) at or above the $5.55B/$3.08 top end with adj operating margin >=8.4%, plus a first formal 2027 revenue framework at or above ~$34B (>65% growth) and confirmation that OpenAI rack initial deliveries shipped in Q4 2026; secondary confirmation is a 2027 adj EPS consensus settling above $17.50 (dilution-adjusted) without the gross margin slipping below the mid-11% band.
dossier.what_kills: Any of: (1) a Q3 or Q4 2026 guide that implies 2027 growth below ~40%, or language that 2027 acceleration has slipped to 2028; (2) a top-3 customer disclosing dual-sourcing or in-house rack integration that cuts Celestica's share; (3) gross margin dropping below 11% because of memory/silicon input inflation; (4) a second equity raise or a sharp working-capital-driven negative FCF quarter, which would confirm the volume beneficiary is funding its customers' growth with shareholder capital.
dossier.balance_sheet: At Jun 30, 2026: cash $535.7M, gross debt $740M, net debt $204M, leverage ~0.3-0.6x, liquidity >$2B after a revolver upsized by $1B with maturities extended to 2031. Pro forma for the Aug 7, 2026 $3.0B equity raise (9.68M shares at $310, before fees; greenshoe of 1.45M shares unconfirmed), net cash is roughly $2.7-2.8B. Cash generation is positive but thin for the growth rate: 2026 FCF guide $600M on $20.5B revenue (~3%), after ~$1B capex; H1 FCF $285M. Dilution risk is now the key balance-sheet issue: shares rose from ~114.98M (Aug 4) to ~124.66M (~8.4%), and management chose equity over debt at 0.3x leverage, signalling either very large 2027 working-capital needs or a desire to fund customers' ramps with a cushion. No cash burn today, but watch inventory and receivables if 2027 revenue exceeds $34B.
dossier.suggested_sizing: Sleeve 1-1.5% of the speculative sleeve now (post-dilution reset, 26% below high, 19-20x implied 2027 EPS); scale to core 2-3% only after the Q3 print (~Oct 26) confirms 2027 growth >65% and the gross margin holds; do not exceed 3% given 65% top-3 customer concentration and demonstrated willingness to issue equity.

dossier.name: Jabil Inc.
dossier.market_cap: ~$32B implied at $305.92 (4 Sep 2026) x ~104.8M shares outstanding; third-party figure was $38.05B in Aug 2026 before the late-August slide (stockanalysis.com)
dossier.business: Jabil is one of the two largest US-listed electronics manufacturing services (EMS) companies: it designs, builds and integrates hardware for other companies' brands across three segments - Intelligent Infrastructure (AI/cloud data-center racks, compute, storage, networking, optics, power, liquid cooling, plus semi capital equipment), Regulated Industries (healthcare, automotive/EV, energy) and Connected Living & Digital Commerce (consumer devices, retail/payment hardware). Customers are hyperscalers (three won to date), OEMs and networking/semicap vendors; the model is high-volume, low-margin assembly (core operating margin ~5.8%) with value-add creeping in via rack-level integration, photonics and cooling.
dossier.why_now: The thesis is not a sold-out-input bottleneck; it is a volume ramp. AI-related revenue is guided to ~$13.6B in FY26 (Aug year-end), up ~50% from $9B in FY25, and management said on the 17 Jun 2026 call that FY27 AI revenue should grow at a similar percentage rate off the larger base (i.e. roughly $20B if taken literally) with core operating margin moving above 6%. Jabil won its third hyperscale customer in Q3 FY26 (a few hundred million dollars of revenue in FY27, scaling toward $1B+ in FY28) and cited ~$500M of incremental demand across racks in its FY26 Intelligent Infrastructure guide. The company has raised its FY26 revenue outlook three times this year ($32.4B -> $34B in March -> $35B in June). What makes it timely: the stock has fallen ~29% from its June intraday high to $305.92 (4 Sep 2026) on no identifiable fundamental change, ahead of the Q4 print on 24 Sep and a September investor briefing that will set FY27 guidance. Note the multiple has already re-rated from the low-teens EMS norm to low-20s forward, so the entry is "cheaper than Celestica," not "cheap."
dossier.analogue: Closest to the Dell analogue - a volume beneficiary of AI server/rack demand on a modest multiple - but only moderately close. Like Dell, Jabil sells assembly/integration capacity into hyperscaler capex at thin margins (5.8% core op margin vs Celestica's 8.4%), earnings are growing ~25-30% rather than the 7x-21x of the bottleneck plays (SanDisk/Micron/Seagate), and there is no sold-out input or price spike in its own P&L; if anything, the memory shortage is a cost/availability risk for Jabil, not a benefit. It differs from Dell in that its multiple has already roughly doubled from its pre-2024 history (~10-12x to ~22-24x forward), so the "low multiple" leg of the analogue is only relative to Celestica (30-38x forward), not absolute. Not a binary readout and not a government-backed turnaround.

input.thesis: Enterprise storage vendor raising prices twice on the NAND shortage; up roughly 64 percent YTD; pricing power with a margin lag.

dossier.name: NetApp, Inc.
dossier.business: NetApp sells enterprise data storage and data-management: ONTAP-based all-flash (AFF) and hybrid arrays, object storage, Keystone storage-as-a-service, and first-party cloud storage services co-sold by the hyperscalers (Azure NetApp Files, FSx for ONTAP, Google Cloud NetApp Volumes). Customers are large enterprises and public-sector buyers, increasingly for AI data-lake modernisation and inference/RAG data pipelines. It is a buyer of NAND flash (from Samsung, Kioxia, Micron, etc.), not a producer, so it sits downstream of the memory bottleneck.

Future customers would be PAH prescribers and payers in a market where Merck's Winrevair did $588M in Q2 2026 (+75% y/y).
dossier.why_now: This is a pure regulatory binary, not a bottleneck. The Phase 3 PROSERA study (topline February 23, 2026) missed its primary endpoint: Hodges-Lehmann placebo-adjusted 6MWD +13.3m, p=0.0320 versus a prespecified alpha of 0.025, so key secondaries could not be formally tested; the stock fell ~80% in a day ($2.13 to $0.42). The setup changed on July 27, 2026 when the company disclosed that FDA Pre-NDA Type B meeting minutes (mid-June meeting) characterised the statistical significance and effect size as "review issues rather than filing issues". Gossamer now intends to file an NDA in September 2026 on one adequate and well-controlled study (PROSERA) plus confirmatory evidence (Phase 2 TORREY, subgroup analyses: North America +25.9m p=0.0573 n=75; intermediate/high-risk +20.0m n=234; CTD-PAH +37.0m p=0.0104 n=87). If accepted (~60 days post-submission, i.e. roughly November 2026), an approval decision could come in Q3 2027. On August 21, 2026 a syndicate (EcoR1, RA Capital, 683, Samsara, Rock Springs, Coastlands) committed up to $250M structured around those two gates: $25M upfront (closed ~August 24), $125M on NDA acceptance, $100M of warrants exercisable only after approval. The next 2-3 months therefore contain a cheap, dated first gate (NDA acceptance) that also unlocks the funding that removes the going-concern problem.
dossier.analogue: Closest to the "binary readout on a washed-out stock" (Moderna) bucket, but only loosely. Similarities: down ~95% from its 52-week high, market cap ~$85M, short interest ~20% of float, dated binary events. Differences that weaken the analogy: the clinical readout has already happened and it missed; what remains is a regulatory judgment call on a p=0.032 result, which historically is a low-probability path. Moderna-style winners had washed-out sentiment but intact fundamentals; here the fundamentals themselves are impaired, the balance sheet is distressed (going-concern language, 7.5% secured converts, Nasdaq delisting clock), and the capital structure means most upside accrues to new preferred/warrant holders rather than common. Not a bottleneck play (SanDisk/Micron), not a low-multiple volume beneficiary (Dell), and not government-backed (Intel). Resemblance: moderate on price pattern, weak on quality.

dossier.bull_case: FDA accepts the NDA in ~November 2026 (the agency already said the p=0.032 result is a review, not a filing, issue), which alone unlocks $125M and removes the going-concern language; the stock could re-rate from ~$0.17 toward the $0.34 exchange-warrant strike or beyond on de-risking. At the Q3 2027 PDUFA, FDA gives weight to the totality of evidence: a positive Phase 2 TORREY on PVR (-96 dynes, p=0.031), a Phase 3 that is directionally positive on 6MWD (+13.3m, p=0.032) and stronger in the prespecified intermediate/high-risk group (+20.0m, n=234), CTD-PAH (+37.0m, p=0.0104) and North America (+25.9m), plus a differentiated inhaled, non-hormonal mechanism for an add-on market where Winrevair is already at $588M/quarter. Even $150-300M of peak seralutinib sales at a 3-5x multiple would support an equity value of $500M-1.5B, which on a ~2-2.5B fully diluted share count is roughly $0.25-0.60/share, i.e. 1.5-3.5x from here, and sell-side targets of $1-4 imply more if dilution is lighter than I assume. Quality sponsors (RA Capital, EcoR1, Samsara, 683) signed up after seeing the FDA minutes, and short interest near 20% of float can fuel sharp squeezes on each gate.
dossier.bear_case: A Phase 3 that missed its primary endpoint at p=0.032 with a 13.3m walk-distance effect (versus ~40m for sotatercept in STELLAR) is a weak approval package; the placebo arm's +13.5m median improvement suggests the drug's incremental benefit is modest, and 13% transaminase elevations >=3x ULN plus 37% cough are real safety/tolerability flags for a chronic inhaled therapy. FDA can accept the file and still issue a CRL or demand a second trial, with an advisory committee likely; the $125M second closing only requires acceptance, so the company gets funded to reach a decision that could still go against it. Chiesi, which had paid $160M for ex-US rights and had full data access, chose to hand the asset back for a $5M payment, a strong negative signal. Even in the good case, common holders sit behind $65M of 7.5% first-lien converts at $0.19, exchange warrants at $0.34, ~$125M of preferred and $100M of approval warrants at $0.187, so most approval value leaks to new capital; a 1:10-1:150 reverse split by October 5, 2026 is likely, and reverse splits in distressed microcaps typically precede further declines. Cash burn was ~$42M in Q2 2026 on a $57M balance; without acceptance by early 2027 the company is back at going-concern with the stock near $0.10. Securities class actions (class period June 16, 2025-February 20, 2026) add legal overhang.
dossier.what_confirms: An 8-K or press release (expected ~November 2026) stating that FDA has accepted the seralutinib NDA for filing, ideally with a standard PDUFA date in Q3 2027 and no refuse-to-file or major amendment request, followed within days by confirmation that the ~$125M second closing has funded. Secondary confirmation: FDA granting priority review or not calling an advisory committee, and a Q3 2026 10-Q that drops the going-concern paragraph.
dossier.what_kills: A refuse-to-file letter, or an acceptance accompanied by FDA stating it will require an additional adequate and well-controlled study; either leaves the $125M and $100M tranches unfunded with ~$60-70M of cash against ~$35-40M quarterly burn. Earlier signals would be slippage of the September NDA submission into Q4 2026, a delisting to OTC after October 5, 2026 without a reverse split, or the full PROSERA dataset (publication/conference) showing the North American and CTD-PAH subgroups were post-hoc or driven by small-n outliers.
dossier.balance_sheet: Cash, equivalents and marketable securities $57.0M at June 30, 2026, down from $99.2M at March 31, 2026 (~$42M decline in the quarter, including exchange-related costs); management guided runway "into Q1 2027" before the August raise, and the Q2 10-Q retains substantial-doubt going-concern language. Debt after the June 4, 2026 exchange: ~$65.2M of 7.50% Convertible Senior Secured First Lien Notes due 2030 (conversion price ~$0.19, i.e. ~5,348 shares per $1,000) plus $18.9M of untendered 5% 2027 notes, roughly $84M face versus $200M before; the exchange also issued up to 317.6M common shares/pre-funded warrants and purchase warrants struck at $0.34. Post-exchange share count 488.8M (August 8, 2026); D. E. Shaw holds 6.0% (29.1M shares) from the exchange. August 21, 2026 private placement: ~$25M pre-funded warrants at $0.1399 (~179M share-equivalents) closed ~August 24; ~$125M of Series A-1 convertible preferred funds only on NDA acceptance (conversion price not found); up to ~$100M of FDA-approval warrants at $0.187 (~535M shares if fully exercised). Dilution risk is therefore extreme: fully diluted shares could exceed 2B on approval, and a reverse split of 1:10 to 1:150 is authorised. Chiesi retains a capped royalty and milestone payments on seralutinib. Cash burn: R&D $26.4M plus G&A $8.9M in Q2 2026 (~$35M/quarter operating), expected to decline further with the RIF; NDA-related and pre-commercial spending could offset that.
dossier.suggested_sizing: Lottery 0.25-0.5% of the speculative sleeve at most, sized so a total loss is immaterial; if taken, prefer entering before the NDA-acceptance gate (~November 2026) and cutting half on acceptance rather than holding the full position through the Q3 2027 PDUFA. Not appropriate for a core or even a standard 1% sleeve position given going-concern status, sub-$1 delisting risk and the multi-layer dilution stack.

input.thesis: INO-3107 pivotal data expected 30 October 2026 with a high estimated probability of success; washed-out stock.

dossier.name: Inovio Pharmaceuticals, Inc.
dossier.market_cap: ~$130-141M (CNBC/companiesmarketcap show ~$140.6M in early Sept 2026; 103.4M shares as of 10 Aug 2026 x $1.25 close on 1 Sept 2026 = ~$129M; one aggregator shows $93M, likely stale). Fully diluted is materially higher: ~67M warrants outstanding from the April ($1.40 strike, 25M) and July ($1.10 strike, 42.1M+) 2026 offerings.
dossier.business: Inovio is a pre-commercial DNA-medicines biotech (Plymouth Meeting, PA; ~112 staff after March 2026 cuts) whose entire equity story is now INO-3107, a DNA immunotherapy delivered by its proprietary electroporation device that trains the immune system against HPV-6/11, the strains that cause recurrent respiratory papillomatosis (RRP), a rare disease in which patients need repeated airway surgeries. The BLA for adult RRP is under FDA review with a 30 Oct 2026 PDUFA date; if approved, customers are US ENT/laryngology centres and specialty pharmacies for a company-cited ~14,000-15,000 US adult patient pool. Revenue today is negligible (FY2025 revenue $65K per stockanalysis); the rest of the pipeline is de-prioritised.
dossier.why_now: The binary is a regulatory decision, not a data readout: the working thesis mislabels 30 Oct 2026 as "pivotal data" when it is the PDUFA action date on an already-filed BLA built on a 32-patient single-arm Phase 1/2 (RRP-001) plus a 28-patient retrospective follow-up (RRP-002). The efficacy data are strong for the indication (72% of patients had a 50-100% cut in surgeries in Year 1; 86% overall response and 50-54% complete response in Years 2-3; mean surgeries fell from 4.1 to 1.7 to 0.9), and the process is nearly complete: late-cycle review meeting done, all pre-licensure inspections done, management expects label negotiations to begin in September 2026. The live risk that makes this a genuine binary is procedural: in the December 2025 file-acceptance letter the FDA stated its "preliminary conclusion" that Inovio had not justified eligibility for the accelerated approval pathway, and at the July 2026 informal clinical meeting (post CBER/OTP leadership changes) the agency did not revisit that comment and said confirmatory-trial design feedback was still "forthcoming". The stock is washed out for the right reasons: it hit a 52-week low of $0.95 on 28 Jul 2026 on a $20M offering priced at $0.95 with two warrants per share, the 10-Q carries going-concern language, and cash runs only into late Q1 2027. The comparator that makes the prize concrete is Precigen's Papzimeos (approved Aug 2025, first RRP therapy): $21.6M Q1 2026 and $53.1M Q2 2026 net revenue at a ~$400K net price per patient, which proves the market pays for this indication and gives INO-3107 (fewer required scoping procedures during dosing) a defined second-to-market slot.
dossier.analogue: Closest to the Moderna analogue in the framework (binary event on a washed-out stock), and it is a purer, smaller-cap version of it: a ~$130M market cap, ~55-58% below the 52-week high, short interest ~19% of float (April 2026), going-concern language, and a single dated event with an all-or-nothing outcome. It is NOT a bottleneck play (no sold-out input, no pricing power yet, no earnings) and not a government-backed turnaround. The main difference from Moderna is that the event is an FDA action on a thin single-arm dataset with an unresolved pathway-eligibility question rather than a randomized readout, so the "probability of success" is a regulatory judgment, not a statistical one; and unlike Moderna the balance sheet cannot absorb a miss.

dossier.bull_case: FDA approves INO-3107 on or before 30 Oct 2026 with a label comparable to Papzimeos. Precigen has already proven the commercial model: $21.6M in Q1 2026 and $53.1M in Q2 2026 (second and third full quarters on market) at ~$400K net per patient, with >500 patients registered against a US adult prevalence the companies put at ~14,000-15,000. INO-3107 has a differentiated profile (no scoping/surgery required during the dosing window vs 83% of Papzimeos trial patients; 86% response and ~50% complete response at Years 2-3) and a re-dosing strategy under exploration. If Inovio captured even 25% of Precigen's current run-rate that would be ~$50M annualised revenue within a year of launch against a ~$75-100M EV today; a 5x EV/sales on that would imply a market cap several times the current ~$130M even after warrant dilution to ~170M fully diluted shares. Approval also converts the $1.10 and $1.40 warrants (~67M) into ~$80M of non-dilutive-at-a-discount cash and removes the going-concern qualifier, and a ~19% short float would have to cover. Jefferies' $3.00 target (2.3x) is a conservative marker for that scenario.
dossier.bear_case: The FDA issues a CRL on 30 Oct 2026 (or converts the review to a request for a randomized confirmatory trial before approval). The agency put in writing at filing that Inovio had "not submitted adequate information to justify eligibility for the accelerated approval pathway"; at the July 2026 informal meeting it declined to discuss that comment and had not yet given confirmatory-trial design feedback, while CBER/OTP leadership had just changed. The dataset is 32 patients, single-arm, with the durability claim resting on a 28-patient retrospective chart review. With a first-in-class competitor already approved on a 51% complete-response randomized-free dataset, the FDA has less unmet-need pressure to stretch. On a CRL the equity has ~$37M of cash at 30 Sept, a $18M/quarter burn, going-concern language, no debt capacity and 67M warrants that would be worthless: the stock would likely retest and break the $0.95 July low toward the sub-$0.60 prints some data vendors already show, implying 50-70% downside. Even on approval the launch is funded only into late Q1 2027, so another discounted raise precedes any revenue inflection, and Precigen's 12-15 month head start plus patient-hub lock-in could hold INO-3107 to a small share.
dossier.what_confirms: A company statement (most likely at the 9 Sept Cantor fireside or an 8-K) that FDA label negotiations have begun, ideally with confirmation that the agency has accepted accelerated-approval eligibility and has agreed a single-arm confirmatory design; then the approval letter itself on or before 30 Oct 2026 with a broad adult-RRP label.
dossier.what_kills: Any of: (a) September passes with no label-negotiation start and management goes quiet on the eligibility question; (b) an FDA request for a randomized or additional pre-approval trial, an advisory committee, or a PDUFA extension (major amendment) in Sept/Oct; (c) a CRL on 30 Oct 2026. Secondary kill: a further pre-PDUFA equity raise below $1.10, which would signal management is not confident enough to wait for the warrant cash.
dossier.balance_sheet: Cash, equivalents and short-term investments $36.7M at 30 Jun 2026, plus $18.3M net from the July 2026 offering = ~$55M pro forma at end-July; guided Q3 operational burn ~$18M implies ~$37M at 30 Sept 2026. dossier.business: Hudbay is a copper-focused mid-cap miner producing copper concentrate with substantial gold, silver and some zinc by-products from three operating complexes: Constancia (Peru), Snow Lake/Lalor (Manitoba) and Copper Mountain (British Columbia). Customers are smelters and traders; revenue is essentially a function of LME/COMEX copper and spot gold prices times tonnes shipped. Hudbay is a high-margin, net-cash producer whose consolidated cash cost was negative ($(0.40)/lb in Q2, $(1.80)/lb in Q1 thanks to gold at ~$4,300/oz), so nearly every cent of copper price flows to EBITDA. Layered on top is a semi-binary: the Copper World definitive feasibility study (95% of engineering done as of 2026-07-29) and a sanction decision slated for late 2026, which would convert a $1.3B (PFS-era estimate) Arizona project into a funded growth leg with Mitsubishi's $600M already largely in hand. Management projects consolidated copper production +24% in 2027 and +70% by decade-end.
dossier.analogue: Closest to the 2026 'bottleneck play' (SanDisk/Micron/Seagate) but only loosely — perhaps a 40% fit. Copper is a constrained input at a record price, but Hudbay's earnings are up ~50% y/y (Q2 adj EPS $0.28 vs $0.19), not 7-21x, and the multiple has already re-rated (stock +107% over 52 weeks as of mid-July and +154% on TSX over the past year as of early Sept). dossier.name: Hecla Mining Company
dossier.market_cap: ~$14.2B (Investing.com quote page, retrieved 2026-09-06, at $20.68/share)
dossier.business: Hecla is the largest silver producer in the US and Canada, mining silver-lead-zinc and silver-gold concentrates at Greens Creek (Alaska), Lucky Friday (Idaho) and the still-ramping Keno Hill (Yukon), plus Nevada exploration (Midas). It sells concentrates to smelters and traders in the US, Canada, Japan, Korea and China; in Q2 2026 mine revenue was 68% silver, 14% gold and the balance lead/zinc by-products. It sold its Casa Berardi gold mine (Quebec) to Orezone in March 2026 to become a purer silver play; 2025 silver output topped 17 Moz and 2026 guidance is 15.1-16.1 Moz silver plus 51-55 koz gold.
dossier.why_now: The bottleneck is the metal, not the company. Silver is in its sixth consecutive annual supply deficit (Silver Institute, April 2026; cumulative drawdown since 2021 cited at ~762 Moz) and spiked to a nominal all-time high of $121.67/oz on 29 Jan 2026 (up ~65% in January alone after >150% in 2025). Hecla is the highest-beta large US-listed way to own that input: consolidated Q2 2026 cash cost was negative $8.10/oz and AISC $6.07/oz after by-product credits, so roughly 90% of every realized silver dollar dropped to margin, adjusted EBITDA doubled YoY, and the company went from ~$550M net debt to net cash in two quarters. The catch that distinguishes it from the 2026 semis/memory winners: the price spike has already broken. Silver fell >30% in ~30 hours on 29-30 Jan, hit $58.39 in late June (-52% from peak), and sits at ~$66.94 today (6 Sep 2026), so the "sold-out input" is still in deficit but its price is 45% below the high and banks (UBS, JPM, HSBC) have been cutting forecasts citing demand destruction and higher mine supply.
dossier.analogue: Closest to the bottleneck play (Micron/SanDisk/Seagate: scarce input, price spike, earnings step-change), but a weaker, later-cycle version. Similarities: a genuinely supply-constrained input (six-year deficit), earnings up ~2x YoY (Q2 net income +104%, adj. EBITDA $199M vs $94M) and a balance-sheet transformation. Differences that matter: (1) Hecla is a pure price-taker with no backlog, lead times or pricing power, so there is no "sold out" signal the company itself controls; (2) the earnings uplift is ~2x, not 7-21x, because silver already gave back half its spike; (3) volume is going the wrong way (2026 silver guidance 15.1-16.1 Moz vs 17+ Moz in 2025, Keno Hill ramp slowed); (4) the multiple has NOT re-rated up: trailing P/E ~35-42x has compressed to a forward P/E of ~16.8x as earnings caught up. Net: a bottleneck-play analogue at maybe 50-60% fit, sitting where memory names would be if DRAM spot had already crashed 45% from peak while the deficit narrative persisted.

dossier.what_confirms: Silver holding above ~$75-80 into Q4 (retaking the UBS December target) while Q3 results (4 or 11 Nov 2026) show Lucky Friday sustaining ~1.5 Moz/qtr, consolidated AISC still below ~$10/oz, and quarterly FCF back above the $140M Q1 record. A Silver Institute interim update showing the 2026 deficit widening rather than narrowing would validate that January's spike was liquidity-driven rather than demand-destroying.
dossier.what_kills: Silver breaking the late-June low of $58.39 with the Silver Institute or bank research showing the deficit closing (mine-supply response plus industrial substitution), or Hecla cutting 2026 silver guidance again below 15.1 Moz / abandoning the >$700M FCF target. A cash-cost guide back into positive territory as by-product zinc/lead/gold prices fall would also remove the margin cushion the bull case rests on.
dossier.balance_sheet: Cash $483M at 30 Jun 2026 (Q1 sources quote the same figure, so timing is slightly uncertain); no long-term debt outside capital leases after the $263M 7.25% 2028 notes were redeemed on 9 Apr 2026; $225M revolver essentially undrawn. Net position moved from ~$550M net debt to net cash within two quarters, funded by record FCF ($144M Q1, $136M Q2) plus $183.4M net proceeds from the Casa Berardi and Minera Hecla sales; Hecla also holds ~65.8M Orezone shares and up to $321M of deferred/contingent Casa Berardi consideration. No cash burn, no dilution need; conversely no buyback and a nominal $0.015/yr dividend. Diluted share count not found (implied by market cap/price at roughly 690M shares).
dossier.suggested_sizing: Sleeve 1-2% for a risk-aware investor; not a core holding. This is a ~2x-beta call on the silver price that already crashed 52% once this year; size so a repeat of the March or June drawdown (-50% from high) costs under 1% of the book. Scale toward 2-3% only if silver reclaims $80 with Q3 confirming cost/FCF delivery.
